May contain spoilers from Myth-Speaker **Source** [Pathfinder #218: Titanbane ](/Sources.aspx?ID=274) pg. 81 **Price** 150 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L --- This reversible doll shows Iapholi on one side and the [harpy](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3046) Ekriathe who preceded her in her line of reincarnation on the other. Non-magical successor dolls are popular gifts for children, and Iapholi often distributes them (including a handful of magical versions) on her birthday. Magical _successor dolls_ sometimes frown, smile, or wink as if aware of their surroundings and nearby conversations. **Activate—Big Eyes, Pleading Face** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You fail or critically fail to [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=2393) a favor; **Effect** The doll’s eyes grow large as its lips quiver, expressing adorable disappointment. Roll 1d4 and add the result to your [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) check as a circumstance bonus, which might improve the degree of success. **Activate—Fierce Gaze, Approving Smile** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You succeed or critically succeed when [Coercing](/Actions.aspx?ID=2394) a creature; **Effect** The doll smugly smirks at the creature, either reinforcing how wise it is to heed your demands or innocently reminding it how much happier it is for complying. After the creature finishes following your directives, it must attempt a DC 21 Will save. **Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Failure** The creature’s fond memory of the doll’s approval overwhelms any hard feelings the creature has toward you; it doesn’t act against you as a result of your coercion unless your demands were truly shocking (such as forcing them to violate any anathema they have or betray a close ally).

---

This rare and highly addictive drug is rumored to be created by wizards working alongside [succubi](/Monsters.aspx?ID=98). Taken in the form of lozenges, this drug can heighten the body's pleasure and pain stimuli as well as increase alertness, energy, and euphoria. Serious side effects that can occur include heart attack, stroke, and sudden vision and hearing loss, but these risks do little to deter users.

The save for [addiction](/Diseases.aspx?ID=15) to succubus kiss is DC 28, and the addiction has the [virulent](/Traits.aspx?ID=162) trait.

 **Saving Throw** DC 24 Fortitude; **Onset** 1 minute; **Maximum Duration** 8 hours; **Stage 1** +2 item bonus to initiative checks (10 minutes) and to all saving throws against [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60) and [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) effects; **Stage 2** as stage 1 plus [drained 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10) (1 hour); **Stage 3** as stage 2 plus [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) or [deafness](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8) (1 hour); **Stage 4** blindness and deafness (1 hour); **Stage 5** [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38)

---

This _[+1 ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2785) [explorer’s clothing](/Armor.aspx?ID=39)_ is a simple, practical, and unassuming two-piece outfit. The comfortable fabric is enchanted with illusory magic to make it look as if the wearer is wearing heavy armor (as _[_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1568)_). While wearing the suit, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2388) someone who would normally wear heavy armor. 

**Activate—Faux Bulwark** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You strike an intimidating pose that causes enemies to fear your supposedly heavily armored form. Each foe in a 15-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) who can see you must attempt a DC 22 Will saving throw. On a failure, they’re [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1 (frightened 2 on a critical failure).

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 65 **Price** 450 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L --- This metallic tube has a complex array of lenses and prisms at one end and a hatch at the other. The hatch can be unlocked, loaded with a [glow rod](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3355), and refastened using 3 Interact actions. **Activate** ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Requirements** A glow rod is installed in the dazzler; **Effect** The glow rod burns to dust in a single focused flash, creating a 30-foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386) of scintillating light. Each creature in the cone must attempt a DC 24 Fortitude save, with the following effects. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) for 1 round.
**Failure** The creature is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) for 1 round or until it spends an Interact action to rub its eyes, ending the blinded condition.
**Critical Failure** The creature is blinded for 1 round.

</title>

<traits>

---

When you drink this elixir, you physically become as you were in whatever phase of your youth you desire. Your new body begins in peak health, regardless of what your actual condition was at that age. Any physical or mental imperfections— including scars, lost limbs, and curses, diseases, poisons of 20th level or lower— are removed, and you regain your full Hit Points. You immediately begin to age normally again, with your natural lifespan extended as if you had never aged past your new apparent age. You retain all your memories.

 Unlike Crafting most items, brewing the sun orchid elixir takes 1 month’s time. While an individual vial of sun orchid elixir isn’t unique, the formula is unique, and it’s known only to Artokus Kirran of Thuvia.

The process of creating the [sun orchid elixir](/Equipment.aspx?ID=497) leaves behind a large amount of thick paste with its own healing properties. Artokus commonly sells this paste to Thuvian natives who can't purchase the elixir proper and uses the income to support his alchemy students. When you apply the sun orchid poultice, it reduces your [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3), [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10), and [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13) condition values by 2. In addition, the poultice provides a youthful burst of energy, granting you a +3 item bonus to saves and 20 temporary Hit Points for 1 hour.

Placed under the eyes like rays of light, this tattoo burns away illusions with the unmerciful brilliance of the sun. You gain a +2 bonus to Perception checks that involve sight. If you're [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7), you receive a new save at the start of each of your turns to end your dazzled condition.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action to Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The tattoo casts a 4th-rank [_blazing bolt_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1450), with the rays emitting from your eyes. The number of actions you spend Activating the tattoo determines _blazing bolt’s_ number of rays. The tattoo also attempts to dispel each illusion on a creature hit by a ray ([counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) rank 5th, counteract modifier +19).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 5"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Sun Wheel](/Equipment.aspx?ID=905)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Troubles in Otari</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Troubles in Otari](/Sources.aspx?ID=55) pg. 60

**Price** 150 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Created by the priests of a Qadiran sect of [Sarenites](/Deities.aspx?ID=16), the _sun wheels_ were designed to protect the Dawnflower's followers in their quest to hunt down a dangerous cult trying to raise a spawn of the evil god [Rovagug](/Deities.aspx?ID=15). Once they completed their crusade, these priests disbanded and went on to minister other congregations. They each took their _sun wheels_ with them, handing them down to the next generations.

 This copper medallion is etched with a stylized sun, its rays shaped like the spokes of a wagon wheel. It tends to glint brightly when exposed to sunlight. While wearing this pendant, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) checks. You must be good-aligned to use the sun wheel's true power: the following activation, which provides you a shield of burning force.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> concentrate;     **Effect** The _sun wheel_ casts a [_shield_](/Spells.aspx?ID=280) spell benefiting you. When you use the spell to prevent damage, you prevent 10 damage instead of 5. If the attacker is adjacent to you, you can choose to deal 2d6 fire damage to it, which it gets a DC 21 basic Reflex save to resist.

 If you choose to deal the fire damage, you can't Activate _the sun wheel_ again until the next morning. If you prevent damage but don't deal the fire damage, you can use it again in 10 minutes, as normal for _shield_.

</column>

</title>

**Bulk** L

---

This gold-and-ivory incense burner always emits a pleasant, floral-scented smoke without any need to be refilled. It has a chain that can be easily affixed to a belt or bag, allowing it to be worn without a free hand. As long as the censer is burning, the bearer benefits from the [_undetectable alignment_](/Spells.aspx?ID=348) spell. They also don't appear [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) to [divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47) spells or abilities, or to senses such as [lifesense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=21), unless those abilities successfully [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the censer. The censer can be lit or extinguished with an Interact action.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** Smoke bellows from the censer with the effects of an [_obscuring mist_](/Spells.aspx?ID=210) centered on you.

</title>

<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
<trait label="Intelligent" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=280" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 163

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Dragon-Mouth Pistol](/Weapons.aspx?ID=200)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Perception** +12; precise vision 30 feet, imprecise hearing 30 feet

**Communication** speech ([Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1))

**Skills** [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) +19, [Navigation Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +14, Sailing Lore +14

**Int** +0, **Wis** +2, **Cha** +4

**Will** +16 

</column>

---        

A _sunken pistol_ is imbued with the unfulfilled desires and insatiable greed of its previous wielder, a notorious pirate drowned at sea. Once a beautiful and artistically wrought weapon, a _sunken pistol_ is coated in a fine layer of dried salt and encrusted with barnacles. Each shot fired from this _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [dragon mouth pistol](/Weapons.aspx?ID=200)_ is now coated in a layer of salty ectoplasm and has the effects of a [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=297) rune. You can shoot the _sunken pistol_ underwater, even when using black powder ammunition.

---

This sturdy pole has a rope attached to one end in a loop with the other end extending to the handle. You can pull the handle side of the rope to tighten the loop. Using this loop, you can [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) without having a free hand. A creature grappled this way receives a –2 circumstance penalty to attack rolls when [Striking](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with an unarmed attack. Due to limitations in the size of the loop, a catch pole can only be used on creatures sized Medium or smaller.

Supports, also commonly known as braces, can be applied to any of the following major joints: wrist, elbow, knee, and ankle. They typically strap around the desired area and provide not only support but warmth that soothes aches and pains. You can still use your limb or joint even if you're not wearing your support, but you might feel aches and pains that are worse than usual and may manifest into physical symptoms.

---

These sturdy leather boots have warm fur lining and magically augmented steel crampons that offer the wearer purchase on even the slipperiest ice slicks. _Sure-step crampons_ allow you to walk across ice without difficulty, ignoring the uneven ground and difficult terrain caused by ice, and reducing greater difficult terrain caused by ice to ordinary difficult terrain.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;    **Requirements** You're standing on an earthen, icy, or wooden surface; **Effect** You dig the crampons into the spot where you're standing, offering additional support until the next time you move. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your Fortitude or Reflex DC against attempts to [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) or [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40) you. This bonus also applies to saving throws against spells or effects that attempt to [move you](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) or knock you [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). The bonus lasts until you move from your current spot.

The light-brown liquid of a _sure-step potion_ helps you find your footing. </title>

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 147

**Price** 75 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

---

This stick is a decorative wooden baton with a metal cap on one end and a stylized handle in the shape of a horse or other martial beast on the other. Mundane swagger sticks are carried by officers in armies all across Golarion. This one is made of particularly fine wood, with an aged silver cap and handle, and small garnets for the creature’s eyes.

**Activate—Swagger** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You dramatically swing, twirl, or otherwise brandish the _swagger stick_ to direct your troops. All allied creatures within 30 feet who can see your display gain +1 status bonus to attack rolls, Fortitude saves, and Will saves against mental effects for 1 round.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 6+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Swallow-Spike](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1838)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 13

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) Attacks made by armor with the swallow-spike rune apply the Multiple Attack Penalty as if you had made them with another weapon._

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** etched onto armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Your armor responds to your desire to break free of a creature grabbing you by growing spikes.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=540), [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))  **Trigger** You become [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20), [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=33), or otherwise held immobilized in a creature's grasp, such as by being [engulfed](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=14) or [swallowed](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=35);  **Effect** Your armor suddenly grows spikes, attacking the triggering creature. The armor makes a melee attack with an attack modifier of +14 that deals 2d6 piercing damage. <title
    level="1"
    right="Item 3"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Swamp Lily Quilt](/Equipment.aspx?ID=786)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Legends](/Sources.aspx?ID=40) pg. 86

**Price** 12 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Two Actions" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This quilt is defined by its green lily-pad pattern, which is rare in Bellflower communications. The quilt is 10 feet square and infused with a reagent that activates when the quilt is laid out across soil or earth. One round after you lay out the quilt, the ground beneath it becomes soft and muddy, creating difficult terrain in the area where the quilt was. You can leave the quilt to maintain the difficult terrain indefinitely, but the affected ground begins to dry once you remove the quilt with an Interact action. The ground dries over the span of 1 hour, after which the ground returns to normal terrain. Placing the quilt on the ground uses up its infused reagents, and it becomes an ordinary quilt once removed from the ground.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Swarmform Collar](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1326)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Companion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=29" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 55

**Price** 350 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn collar

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This sturdy leather collar is imprinted with tessellated animal shapes. When invested, the animal shapes change to match that of your companion.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You touch the collar and your companion splits into a swarm of hundreds of identical Tiny versions of itself for 1 minute. Its space becomes Large, it gains the weaknesses and resistances of a [spider swarm](/Monsters.aspx?ID=385), and the [swarm](/Traits.aspx?ID=707) trait, though it doesn't gain [swarm mind](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=36), as it's controlled by a single mind. Its unarmed attacks are replaced with a single-action swarming attack that deals 1d8 damage of the type normally inflicted by the companion's unarmed attacks to any foe in its space, with a DC 23 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save. While in swarm form, your companion can take the Support action but can't perform its advanced maneuver. Its other statistics don't change. If the companion is reduced to 0 Hit Points while in swarm form, the companion immediately recombines into its original form in an available space, in addition to the usual effects of being reduced to 0 Hit Points.

</column>

    right="Item 4"

>
[Sweet Hag's Eye](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4946)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Troubles in Grayce</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=662" />
<trait label="Scrying" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=689" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Troubles in Grayce](/Sources.aspx?ID=327) pg. 118

**Price** 75 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This item appears to be a normal, if admittedly macabre, piece of hard peppermint candy the size and shape of a human eyeball. That's because it is actually the eye of a [sweet hag](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3041), removed and painstakingly replaced with a mix of enchantment and cookery. It is typically mounted on a piece of jewelry or stored in a small sack worn on a cord.

 The eye provides no direct benefit for the wearer, but the hag whose eye it once was can peer through it using the [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) action, and cast the [_message_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1598) cantrip through it onto the creature carrying the eye. Both these effects have no range limited, provided the hag is on the same plane.

 Any damage to the eye destroys it. The sweet hag can also choose to destroy the eye remotely using Meltaway Mint. The eye can also be eaten, but a creature who attempts this is exposed to sickeningly sweet. 

**Activate—Meltaway Mint** <actions string="Single Action" /> ;     **Effect** The hag causes the eye to melt away under a brief flare of intense heat. If a creature is holding the eye, they must attempt a DC 18 Reflex save. On a failure, they take 1d4 [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) as the boiling hot candy remains stick to and burn their skin.

 **Sickeningly Sweet** ([ingested](/Traits.aspx?ID=633), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669)) The [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) condition caused by this poison can't be ended until the poison's effects end; **Saving Throw** DC 20 Fortitude; **Onset** 1 minute; **Maximum Duration** 10 minutes; **Stage 1** sickened 1 (1 minute); **Stage 2** 1d8 poison damage and sickened 2 (1 minute); **Stage 3** 2d8 poison damage and sickened 3 (1 minute)

**Craft Requirements** You must be a sweet hag.

</column>

fields.text: Item 4 Sweet Hag's Eye May contain spoilers from Troubles in Grayce Rare Occult Scrying Source Troubles in Grayce pg. 118 Price 75 gp Usage worn This item appears to be a normal, if admittedly macabre, piece of hard peppermint candy the size and shape of a human eyeball. That's because it is actually the eye of a sweet hag, removed and painstakingly replaced with a mix of enchantment and cookery. It is typically mounted on a piece of jewelry or stored in a small sack worn on a cord. The eye provides no direct benefit for the wearer, but the hag whose eye it once was can peer through it using the Seek action, and cast the message cantrip through it onto the creature carrying the eye. Both these effects have no range limited, provided the hag is on the same plane. Any damage to the eye destroys it. The sweet hag can also choose to destroy the eye remotely using Meltaway Mint. The eye can also be eaten, but a creature who attempts this is exposed to sickeningly sweet. Activate—Meltaway Mint Single Action ; Effect The hag causes the eye to melt away under a brief flare of intense heat. If a creature is holding the eye, they must attempt a DC 18 Reflex save. On a failure, they take 1d4 persistent fire damage as the boiling hot candy remains stick to and burn their skin. Sickeningly Sweet (ingested, poison) The sickened condition caused by this poison can't be ended until the poison's effects end; Saving Throw DC 20 Fortitude; Onset 1 minute; Maximum Duration 10 minutes; Stage 1 sickened 1 (1 minute); Stage 2 1d8 poison damage and sickened 2 (1 minute); Stage 3 2d8 poison damage and sickened 3 (1 minute) Craft Requirements You must be a sweet hag.

_Swirling sand_ carries a faint trace of strange compulsions from the helical sand spire near Beachcomber. Adding this catalyst to a [_suggestion_](/Spells.aspx?ID=315) spell implants a strange compulsion in one target of the spell. The target creature must spin counterclockwise at the end of its turn if it didn't take a [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114) action that turn. This spin is a free action that has the move trait. This effect lasts for 3 rounds on a success, failure, or critical failure against suggestion (even if the target completes its suggestion in fewer rounds); a target that critically succeeds against _suggestion_ is unaffected by the _swirling sand_.

fields.text: Item 7 Swirling Sand Rare Catalyst Consumable Magical Source Dark Archive (Remastered) pg. 72 Price 52 gp Usage held in 1 hand Bulk L Activate Cast a Spell Swirling sand carries a faint trace of strange compulsions from the helical sand spire near Beachcomber. Adding this catalyst to a suggestion spell implants a strange compulsion in one target of the spell. The target creature must spin counterclockwise at the end of its turn if it didn't take a move action that turn. This spin is a free action that has the move trait. This effect lasts for 3 rounds on a success, failure, or critical failure against suggestion (even if the target completes its suggestion in fewer rounds); a target that critically succeeds against suggestion is unaffected by the swirling sand .

This tarnished necklace can be attuned only by someone who is holy or unholy. When you attune it, it transforms into your deity's religious symbol or a personal symbol if you don't have a deity. You receive a +1 item bonus to Religion and a +1 circumstance bonus to saves against holy and unholy effects. 

**Activate—Presence** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The symbol casts [_bane_](/Spells.aspx?ID=18) or [_bless_](/Spells.aspx?ID=25). The counteract DC of these effects is 18, and the counteract modifier is +8.

**Craft Requirements**  You must be holy or unholy.

    level="1"
    right="Item 8"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Tablet of Chained Souls](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1647)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 161

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Half-formed, unreadable runes drift across this weathered stone tablet, which resembles a tombstone too eroded to be legible. Created by a long-dead order of scholars dedicated to [Pharasma](/Deities.aspx?ID=14), the _tablet of chained souls_ can be a powerful tool in laying uneasy spirits to rest, but its magic exacts a heavy cost.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;     **Effect** You present the tablet to a [ghost](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=51), or lay it on a haunted site. The tablet's words resolve into a cryptic but accurate clue about the unfinished business that keeps this spirit from rest. Upon reading the tablet's words, you are subject to a [_geas_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=12) that requires you to right that wrong and lay the ghost to rest. If you die without completing the task, you become a ghost, cursed to remain until another recovers the tablet and discharges your duty.

</column>

Created by a long-dead order of scholars dedicated to Pharasma, the tablet of chained souls can be a powerful tool in laying uneasy spirits to rest, but its magic exacts a heavy cost. Activate Two Actions envision, Interact; Effect You present the tablet to a ghost, or lay it on a haunted site. The tablet's words resolve into a cryptic but accurate clue about the unfinished business that keeps this spirit from rest. Upon reading the tablet's words, you are subject to a geas that requires you to right that wrong and lay the ghost to rest. If you die without completing the task, you become a ghost, cursed to remain until another recovers the tablet and discharges your duty.

**Activate—Spirit Carving** <actions string="Three Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561),[manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** You present the tablet to a [ghost](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=418) or lay it on a haunted site. The tablet's words resolve into a cryptic but accurate clue about the spirit's unfinished business. Upon reading the tablet's words, you're subject to a [_geas_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=118) that requires you to right that wrong and lay the ghost to rest. If you die without completing the task, you become a ghost, cursed to remain until another recovers the tablet and discharges your duty.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Plant" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=125" />
<trait label="Wood" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=508" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 202

**Price** 12 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Two Actions" /><row>([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Harvested from one of the rainbow fields of the [Plane of Wood](/Planes.aspx?ID=25), this cotton boll is filled with multicolored fibers. When you Activate the boll, you make a request for a bespoke set of non-magical [explorer's clothing](/Armor.aspx?ID=2) or [fine clothing](/Equipment.aspx?ID=15). The hard fibers and seeds leap from your hand to spin and weave, cotton flying through the air at incredible speed to make cloth and thread. The clothing is ready at the start of your next turn, in the most convenient spot nearby for hanging the clothing or laying it flat.

 If you hold clothing in your other hand when you activate the boll, the boll instead reweaves that item to match the style you specified. This can't change the type of item; you couldn't turn fine clothing into explorer's clothing or winter clothing, for example.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Convocation</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rival Academies](/Sources.aspx?ID=235) pg. 57

**Price** 1,250 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn shoes

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

---

These stylish shoes were originally created by the Tappin’ Toes Troupe, a group of tap-dancing Taldan bards who achieved massive popularity for their line dance routines. Notoriously lazy when it came to practicing choreography, the troupe enchanted their footwear to enhance their agility. Upon retirement, the troupe sold off their shoe designs, and talented tap shoes have become popular among professional dancers ever since. While wearing the shoes, you gain a +2 item bonus to Acrobatics checks to [Balance](/Actions.aspx?ID=2369) and [Tumble Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=2370) an enemy’s space and to Performance checks using dance.

**Activate—Strut Your Stuff** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You click the toes of your _talented tap shoes_ on the ground, and for the next minute, whenever you succeed or critically succeed at a Reflex save to avoid a damaging effect, you can Stride half your Speed as a reaction. However, during this time, you take a –2 item penalty to Stealth checks to [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=2405).

<title

    right="Item 10+"

>
[Tales in Timber](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2648)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Wood" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=508" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 202

**Price** 850 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Wooden Breastplate](/Armor.aspx?ID=36)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Dozens of pictorial stories—told in wood carvings, painting, or pyrography—adorn every outer surface of this _+1 [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=279) [wooden breastplate](/Armor.aspx?ID=36)_. All are old, and many truly ancient, depicting tales set eons ago on the [Plane of Wood](/Planes.aspx?ID=25). You gain a +2 item bonus to [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) checks to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26). If you know the [_collective memories_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=15) ritual, you can use Nature instead of [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) if you're the primary caster.

**Activate—Statue Disguise** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The armor makes you look like a wooden statue version of one of the creatures depicted on the armor for 1 hour. This is a 3rd-rank [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=159), but it can make you look like any creature depicted on the armor. This doesn't change your size or the capabilities of your body, and it scales the appearance of the creature to match yours. You can Dismiss the activation. <title
    level="1"
    right="Item 11"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Talespinner's Lyre](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2127)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Auditory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=16" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Olfactory" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=246" />
<trait label="Visual" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=163" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 98

**Price** 235 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Two Actions" /><row>([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Plucking a _talespinner's lyre_ while focusing on an event you witnessed causes the instrument to create an illusion in a 50-foot emanation that plays out your memory of the event in real time, complete with sights, sounds, and smells. You can Sustain the Activation for up to 1 minute to keep it playing. The scene reproduces only what's in its area, including nothing beyond that even if present in the memory. The scene is realistic, but all observers can clearly tell it's an illusion. Observers can't interact with the scene directly nor can they taste or touch elements of it to get a sensation you didn't personally experience, but they can attempt skill checks to discern more about the scene without altering its contents. For example, no one could see something you didn't, such as the true form of a creature polymorphed into a squirrel, but an observer might be able to use Perception and [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=85) to discern the squirrel was acting unlike a squirrel should.

 Once the magic is used, the lyre remains as a non-magical [virtuoso instrument](/Equipment.aspx?ID=37).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

    level="1"
    right="Item 9"
    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Taleteller's Ring](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1648)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 161

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn ring

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Smiling faces are inscribed about this silver band. You become a fluent weaver of fictions, gaining a +2 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to [Lie](/Actions.aspx?ID=47), Deception DCs against [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=85), and [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks for storytelling. Whenever you're under suspicion or being questioned by an authority figure, you find yourself compulsively spinning absurd, tall tales that are so unconvincing that they make you look guilty even when you're innocent. The ring's bonuses vanish, and any listener can quickly determine you're lying. Nevertheless, you're completely unable to be honest in such situations.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 117

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

**Access** Member of the Pathfinder Society.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This thin leather cord bears delicate runic markings and threads through an item that can bear affixed [talismans](/Equipment.aspx?Category=15&Subcategory=19). When you [Affix a Talisman](/Actions.aspx?ID=520) to that item, you can thread the talisman onto the cord, activating the cord's preserving effects. The cord is attuned to a particular school of magic, chosen when the cord was created. It gains the corresponding trait for that school. When you activate a talisman threaded through a cord with the same magic school trait that's also the cord's level or lower, attempt a DC 16 flat check. On a success, that talisman is not consumed and can be used again.

When you [Affix a Talisman](/Actions.aspx?ID=520) to that item, you can thread the talisman onto the cord, activating the cord's preserving effects. The cord is attuned to a particular school of magic, chosen when the cord was created. It gains the corresponding trait for that school. When you activate a talisman threaded through a cord with the same magic school trait that's also the cord's level or lower, attempt a DC 16 flat check. On a success, that talisman is not consumed and can be used again.

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Gamemastery Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=22) pg. 113

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This loop of adamantine can be slung on a chain to be worn as a necklace, but must be held to convey its benefits. A creature that can’t cast either arcane or occult spells takes 8d6 mental damage just from picking up the item, and they take that damage again at the start of each of their turns if they continue to hold it. 

If the wielder can cast arcane or occult spells, they can use the talisman of the sphere to more easily control a _[sphere of annihilation](/Equipment.aspx?ID=620)_. This reduces the DC of the check to control the sphere or Sustain the Activation by 10.

**Destruction** The talisman of the sphere is destroyed if touched by a sphere of annihilation.

---

The bright red tassels of the creature known as Taljjae are a ubiquitous motif in Hwanggot and are used as charms to pray for good fortune and reward for great effort. They adorn clothing, weapons, and even drinking gourds. These particular tassels carry within them a potent fraction of the mysterious fey's power. When you activate a _Taljjae tassel_, your weapon gains the properties of the [grievous](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2841) rune for the duration of the triggering attack.

---

A mixture of rendered animal fat and acids designed to ignite the fat when exposed to air, a tallow bomb creates a splash of burning oil that adheres to skin, clothes, and hair. A tallow bomb deals the listed fire damage, [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29), and splash damage. On a critical hit, a living creature taking persistent fire damage from a tallow bomb is [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34) from the stench of burning fat and can't reduce its sickened value below 1 while the persistent fire damage lasts. Many types of tallow bombs grant an item bonus to attack rolls.

>
[Tallowheart Mass](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1738)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Crown of the Kobold King</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=89" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Crown of the Kobold King](/Sources.aspx?ID=148) pg. 117

**Price** 425 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This disgusting mass of magically-infused hardened tallow is often found divided into three portions, each attached to the other by a thin tangle of fibers and hair. While some create _tallowheart masses_ that are connected via lengths of scented cord or even fine chain, the mass of tallow is always off-putting in texture, scent, and appearance. Despite the mass's unpleasant look, this magical item can be quite helpful. Each of the three portions can be activated in one of three ways, but once a portion is activated, it's consumed. Once you've consumed all three portions, you fully expend the _tallowheart mass_.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** If you rub a portion between your hands, the mass melts into your flesh and you gain the [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=32) condition for 1 minute. You can use the extra action each round only for Strike actions made with weapons you wield in your hands.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** If you consume a portion, you regain 4d8+12 Hit Points.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** If you rub a portion on your body, it melts into your worn gear and flesh and grants you resistance 10 to fire damage for 1 minute.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

This large _[+2 striking ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2861) [standard-grade silver ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2920) [bastard sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=370)_ is the signature weapon of many veteran Eagle Knights. It’s easily recognized by its distinctively notched blade and the stylized wings adorning its cross guard. These blades are sometimes passed down from generation to generation.

**Activate—Defense of Liberty** <actions string="Reaction" /> ;  **Frequency** once per hour; **Trigger** You or your mount are targeted by a physical melee or ranged attack; **Requirements** You are aware of the attack and are not [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) against it; **Effect** You or your mount gain a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack.

Eagle Knights charged with protecting Andoran’s western border against Chelaxian incursion often carry these _+2 greater striking standard-grade silver bastard swords_, enchanted to offer greater utility when battling fiends. A greater talonstrike blade gains the Grasping Talons activation.

---

A tanglefoot bag is filled with sticky substances. When you hit a creature with a tanglefoot bag, that creature takes a status penalty to its Speeds for 1 minute. Many types of tanglefoot bag also grant an item bonus on attack rolls.

 On a critical hit, a creature in contact with a solid surface becomes stuck to the surface and immobilized for 1 round, and a creature flying via wings has its wings tangled, causing it to fall safely to the ground and become unable to Fly again for 1 round. Tanglefoot bags are not effective when used on a creature that is in water.

 The target can end any effects by Escaping or spending a total of 3 [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=80) actions to carefully remove the sticky substances. These Interact actions don’t have to be consecutive, and other creatures can provide the actions as well.

A tanglefoot bag is filled with sticky substances. When you hit a creature with a tanglefoot bag, that creature takes a status penalty to its Speeds for 1 minute. Many types of tanglefoot bag also grant an item bonus on attack rolls.

 On a critical hit, a creature in contact with a solid surface becomes stuck to the surface and immobilized for 1 round, and a creature flying via wings has its wings tangled, causing it to fall safely to the ground and become unable to Fly again for 1 round. </title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 65

**Price** 50 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This portable nozzle-and-trigger assembly based on spider spinnerets can extrude and weave alchemical adhesives into temporary constructions. As an [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) action, you can attach a [tanglefoot bag](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3295) to the extruder. A loaded tanglefoot extruder can be activated to consume the attached tanglefoot bag and convert it into a 30-foot rope, whip, or net, depending on the nozzle die you choose when activating the device. The created object lasts for 1 hour. The DC to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) a created rope (if used to bind a creature) or net is equal to the consumed tanglefoot bag’s DC and Escaping destroys the created object.

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 306 **Price** 600 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Activate**([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) --- This thin golden candle bears the symbol of a specific deity emblazoned on its surface, surrounded by the iconography of that deity's faith. A _taper of sanctification_ must be dedicated to a deity who can be sanctified to [holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517) or [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521), and has the corresponding trait. You can attach these light-brown leather flaps adorned with gold stitching to a breastplate or even clothing to protect your upper legs in battle. They give you the freedom to move your body to its limit without worrying about exposing yourself to a hit. While wearing the _tasset of flexibility_, you gain a +1 item bonus to [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) checks.

Make a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with a melee weapon, increasing your [reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=684) by 5 feet for that Strike.

Devised to bypass detection, a dose of taster's folly consists of two compounds that aren't mixed but placed in the contents of one meal. Each compound is harmless on its own. The DC to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) about this poison from one of its components is 23 and attempts to use magic to detect the unmixed components require a successful DC 23 [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check. The onset period begins only if a victim consumes both compounds during the same hour. If the two compounds mix prior to consumption, they become toxic and are detectable as such. The [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34) condition can't be ended until the poison's effects end.

---

A _tattletale orb_ is a polished crystal sphere that appears to function as a [_crystal ball_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=253). If those whom you use the orb to scry on roll better than a critical failure on their saving throw, they receive a telepathic message alerting them to the scrying. A success or better at the save allows the target to choose to allow you to scry anyway, knowing they can use an aspect of the orb against you, according to the orb's type. A creature that rolls a critical success on the saving throw also learns your name and location. Once you Activate a _tattletale orb_ or use it to cast one of your scrying spells, it fuses to you. You must succeed at a Will save, using the scrying Will DC of a _crystal ball_ of the orb's type, to use another such device.

 _Tattletale orbs_ come in the same types as _crystal balls_, with the same activations and powers. However, your target must roll a critical failure on the saving throw for the orb to function as normal for that type of _crystal ball_.

<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Scrying" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=141" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 193

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A _tattletale orb_ is a polished crystal sphere that appears to function as a [crystal ball](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3019). If those whom you use the orb to [scry](/Traits.aspx?ID=689) on roll better than a critical failure on their saving throw, they receive a telepathic message alerting them to the scrying. A success or better at the save allows the target to choose to allow you to scry anyway, knowing they can use an aspect of the orb against you, according to the orb’s type. A creature that rolls a critical success on the saving throw also learns your name and location. Once you Activate a _tattletale orb_ or use it to cast one of your scrying spells, it fuses to you. You must succeed at a Will save, using the scrying Will DC of a _crystal ball_ of the orb’s type, to use another such device.

_Tattletale orbs_ come in the same types as _crystal balls_, with the same activations and powers. However, your target must roll a critical failure on the saving throw for the orb to function as normal for that type of _crystal ball._

fields.text: Item 14+ Tattletale Orb Rare Cursed Magical Scrying Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 193 Usage held in 1 hand Bulk 1 A tattletale orb is a polished crystal sphere that appears to function as a crystal ball . If those whom you use the orb to scry on roll better than a critical failure on their saving throw, they receive a telepathic message alerting them to the scrying. A success or better at the save allows the target to choose to allow you to scry anyway, knowing they can use an aspect of the orb against you, according to the orb's type. A creature that rolls a critical success on the saving throw also learns your name and location. Once you Activate a tattletale orb or use it to cast one of your scrying spells, it fuses to you. You must succeed at a Will save, using the scrying Will DC of a crystal ball of the orb's type, to use another such device. Tattletale orbs come in the same types as crystal balls , with the same activations and powers. However, your target must roll a critical failure on the saving throw for the orb to function as normal for that type of crystal ball . Item 14 Tattletale Orb (Clear Quartz) Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 193 Bulk 1 Item 15 Tattletale Orb (Selenite) Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 193 Bulk 1 The target is temporarily immune to the orb’s see the unseen for 24 hours and can choose to be invisible to the orb’s scrying during that time. Item 16 Tattletale Orb (Moonstone) Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 193 Bulk 1 The target is temporarily immune to the orb's mind reading for 24 hours and can use mind reading against you instead, as if the target used the orb. Item 17 Tattletale Orb (Peridot) Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 193 Bulk 1 The target can send you one telepathic demand . Item 19 Tattletale Orb (Obsidian) Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 193 Bulk 1 The target is temporarily immune to the orb’s truesight for 24 hours. During that time, you see a false vision of the target’s choice if you scry on the target. Despite being higher rank than the spell, you can’t disbelieve this illusion if scrying through the orb.

>
[Tattletale Orb](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4919)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Cursed" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=274" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Scrying" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=141" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 193

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A _tattletale orb_ is a polished crystal sphere that appears to function as a [crystal ball](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3019). If those whom you use the orb to [scry](/Traits.aspx?ID=689) on roll better than a critical failure on their saving throw, they receive a telepathic message alerting them to the scrying. A success or better at the save allows the target to choose to allow you to scry anyway, knowing they can use an aspect of the orb against you, according to the orb’s type. A creature that rolls a critical success on the saving throw also learns your name and location. Once you Activate a _tattletale orb_ or use it to cast one of your scrying spells, it fuses to you. You must succeed at a Will save, using the scrying Will DC of a _crystal ball_ of the orb’s type, to use another such device.

_Tattletale orbs_ come in the same types as _crystal balls_, with the same activations and powers. However, your target must roll a critical failure on the saving throw for the orb to function as normal for that type of _crystal ball._

_Tattletale orbs_ come in the same types as _crystal balls_, with the same activations and powers. However, your target must roll a critical failure on the saving throw for the orb to function as normal for that type of _crystal ball._

May contain spoilers from Extinction Curse **Source** [Pathfinder #156: The Apocalypse Prophet](/Sources.aspx?ID=36) pg. 69 **Usage** worn necklace **Bulk** L --- This gold necklace sports six bails, each with a different _[aeon stone](/Equipment.aspx?ID=407)_. The backside of each bail is engraved with a single ancient [Azlanti](/Languages.aspx?ID=49) rune: Patience, Remembrance, Resilience, Tenacity, Wisdom, Invention. While a bail is active, you recall pieces of childhood memories, brief stories and lessons spoken to you by Aroden. The knowledge imparted by each bail carries a specific power but also allows you to access the invested and resonant powers of the _aeon stone_ in the active bail's slot as though the stone orbited your head. Each day at dawn, a new bail becomes active; roll 1d6 to determine which bail is active, determined by the table below. Only one bail can be active at any time. Once per day, you can attempt to exchange the _aeon stone_ in a given bail for another _aeon stone_ with a successful DC 35 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) check. ##
**D6****Bail****Default _Aeon Stone_**
1PatienceGold nodule
**Active Power**: Telepathy with a range of 100 feet
2RemembranceTourmaline sphere
**Active Power**: Cast [_hypercognition_](/Spells.aspx?ID=156) at will
3ResilienceClear spindle
**Active Power**: Worn armor gains the [_antimagic_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=282) property rune
4TenacityPink rhomboid
**Active Power**: Wielded weapons gain the [_vorpal_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=308) property rune
5WisdomOrange prism
**Active Power**: Skill checks for [downtime](/Traits.aspx?ID=49) activities or to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) are one degree of success higher
6InventionLavender and green ellipsoid
**Active Power**: You can craft items up to 5 levels higher than your actual level
 **Destruction** The memories and lessons that echo through the _Tears of the Last Azlanti_ give clues about steps needed to destroy the artifact. After you have gained the power of each of the six aeon stones at least once, you are granted visions of six locations across Golarion. At each of these locations, you must replace one of the necklace's aeon stones with a _dull gray aeon stone_. Once the final stone is replaced, the powers of the necklace are drawn into its new stones. These stones become pieces of throneglass, and the chain and bails disintegrate.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Gatewalkers</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #189: Dreamers of the Nameless Spires](/Sources.aspx?ID=195) pg. 75

**Price** 1,950 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn gloves

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

---

Copper cables run from these thick leather gloves to nodes that attach to the wearer's temples, allowing a spellcaster to convert the magic they normally cast to pure psychic intention. When you Cast a Spell using the _telekinetic converters_, you substitute any verbal spellcasting components for mental components of simple thought, granting the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait to the spell you're casting.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;     **Effect** You cast [_telekinetic projectile_](/Spells.aspx?ID=334) as an occult cantrip, heightened to a spell level equal to half your level rounded up.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;     **Effect** You cast your choice of [_telekinetic haul_](/Spells.aspx?ID=332) or [_telekinetic maneuver_](/Spells.aspx?ID=333) as a 5th-level occult spell, consuming one of your unexpended spell slots of the same level as if you had used it to cast the spell.

---

Copper cables run from these thick leather gloves to nodes that attach to the wearer’s temples, allowing a spellcaster to convert the magic they normally cast to pure psychic intention. When you Cast a Spell using the _telekinetic converters_, you substitute any spoken words for simple thoughts, granting the [subtle](/Traits.aspx?ID=522) trait to the spell you’re casting.

**Activate—Mental Fling** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))   **Requirements** You have a spellcasting class feature and you can cast cantrips; **Effect** You cast [_telekinetic projectile_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1718) as an [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) [cantrip](/Traits.aspx?ID=550), heightened to a spell rank equal to half your level rounded up.

**Activate—Over Matter** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))   **Requirements** You have a spellcasting class feature and have an unexpended spell slot of 5th rank or higher; **Effect** You cast your choice of [_telekinetic haul_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1716) or [_telekinetic maneuver_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1717) as a 5th-rank occult spell, consuming one of your unexpended spell slots of the same rank as if you had used it to cast the spell.

>
[Temperbrand](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3489)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Prey for Death</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=723" />
<trait label="Fire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=604" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Prey for Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=231) pg. 102

**Price** 70,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Maul](/Weapons.aspx?ID=388)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

When the mighty fire-and-metal elemental Temperbrand is defeated, their corpse transforms into a _+3 major striking [greater flaming](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2838) [grievous](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2841) [shifting](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2846) [maul](/Weapons.aspx?ID=388)_ made of what appears to be molten steel, though it behaves as if it were made of solid metal. When a creature first picks up Temperbrand, they must succeed at a DC 43 Will save to establish their dominance over the weapon. On a success, they become Temperbrand's only accepted wielder and may use the weapon normally. On a failure, the character takes 20d6 fire damage (40d6 fire damage on a critical failure) and drops the weapon as it melts away into slag and immediately reforms in an adjacent space. A new attempt to establish dominance can be made by picking the weapon up again and attempting a new Will save. Once Temperbrand has an accepted wielder, it can't be wielded by anyone else unless the accepted wielder intentionally permits it, declaring so in a loud voice; this permission can be rescinded in a similar manner. Anyone else trying to wield Temperbrand after it has accepted a wielder takes fire damage and causes the weapon to melt away as if they failed the Will save to wield it.

 The additional fire damage caused by Temperbrand's greater flaming property (but not its persistent fire damage) is splash damage. Temperbrand's wielder is immune to this splash damage. 

**Activate—Molten Smash** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You smash Temperbrand against the ground or another solid adjacent surface, causing an explosion of molten metal and force to radiate outward in a 20-foot emanation. All creatures in this area take 10d6 fire damage and 6d6 force damage (DC 43 basic Reflex save); those who critically fail this save are knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88). You are immune to the effects of Molten Smash, but your allies are not.

</column>

This glass bottle holds breezes captured from the heart of the Plane of Air. When you inhale the bottle’s contents, the air fills your lungs so completely that you no longer need to breathe, at least for a time. While the effect lasts, you also gain a status bonus against inhaled threats, such as inhaled poisons. If you spend 1 [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323) when you activate the _day’s breath_, you inhale so deeply that you increase the effect’s duration.

On a successful Strike, a tenderizer grenade deals the listed acid damage to the target and the listed acid splash damage. Any [resistances](/Rules.aspx?ID=2893) the target has against bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage are reduced by an amount based on the bomb’s type. In addition, the target is showered with appetizing esters, oils, and salts, making them [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) against jaws Strikes, fangs Strikes, or similar Strikes with a creature’s mouth. These additional effects last until the end of your next turn, or for 1 minute on a critical hit.

<title

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Tentacle Cannon](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1172)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 156

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A tentacle cannon is a _+1 striking weapon_, built using components from squids, [krakens](/Monsters.aspx?ID=275), and sometimes even stranger tentacled creatures like [alghollthu](/Languages.aspx?ID=24). It's a distinct type of martial firearm that deals 1d8 piercing damage. It has the [capacity 5](/Traits.aspx?ID=399), [concussive](/Traits.aspx?ID=401), and [fatal d12](/Traits.aspx?ID=178) traits, a [range increment](/Traits.aspx?ID=248) of 30 feet, and [reload 2](/Traits.aspx?ID=254). The weapon itself resembles a five-barreled handheld cannon with each barrel made from a hollowed out tentacle.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** You cause one of the tentacles forming the weapon's five barrels to stretch out and attempt to pull and grab a creature within 15 feet. The tentacle attempts to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=35) with a +13 bonus. It can attempt to Grapple any creature, regardless of size. On a success, the tentacle [pulls](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) the creature up to 10 feet directly towards you, until it's in a square adjacent to you.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))   **Requirements** The _tentacle cannon_ has a creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20); **Effect** You continue to keep the _tentacle cannon'_s hold on one creature it has grabbed. Attempt another check to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=35) the creature with a +13 bonus.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** The cannon fires a spray of ink in a 15-foot cone. Creatures in the area must attempt a DC 23 Reflex save. On a failure, the creature is covered in ink and becomes [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) for 1 round and [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) for 1 minute or until it removes the ink. On a critical failure, the creature becomes blinded and dazzled; both conditions last for 1 minute or until it removes the ink. The creature, or an adjacent creature, can use an Interact action to remove the ink from its eyes to remove the blinded and dazzled conditions.

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include the tentacles and ink glands of a creature with a tentacle Strike and ink.

>
[Tentacle Potion](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2095)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Potion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=130" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 91

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Upon consuming this mottled, foul-tasting liquid, the _tentacle potion_ causes you to extrude a long, flexible limb of ectoplasm. Your clothing doesn't need to accommodate this limb of ghostly matter, which can extrude through your clothing and armor. The limb lasts 1 hour, and you can Dismiss the activation. You can't hide or disguise the tentacle. You can use the limb to perform simple Interact actions, such as opening an unlocked door. Your limb can't perform actions that require significant manual dexterity, including any action that would require a check to accomplish. You can't use it to hold items. At one time, you can have only one extra limb from any version of this potion. Stronger tentacle potions replace the effects of weaker ones.

 If you have the [Flexible Tail](/Feats.aspx?ID=2405) or [Skillful Tail](/Feats.aspx?ID=1386) feats, the [Tailed Goblin](/Heritages.aspx?ID=37) heritage, or a similar feature the GM believes would benefit, this potion can instead fortify your tail. A fortified tail benefits from any _tentacle potion_ as if the potion were the next better type.

While using your limb this way, you have free use of all your other limbs, so you can perform tasks that require both hands. This potion lasts 8 hours.

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 124

<row gap="medium">
**Base Shield** [Tower Shield](/Shields.aspx?ID=20)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This [tower shield](/Shields.aspx?ID=20) (Hardness 5, HP 20, BT 10) sports a bright red front with a gold inlay of an eagle. While it looks unassuming, this shield can protect not only yourself but also those behind you.

**Activate—Tortoise Form** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=610), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Your shield creates a magical barrier, consisting of translucent copies of the shield. The barrier is created with the Hardness and Hit Points equal to those of the _testudo shield_ and is [immune to critical hits](/Rules.aspx?ID=2314) and precision damage.

---

This stubby, black candle has a wick made of a type of flammable bronze that can be found only on the [Plane of Fire](/Planes.aspx?ID=6). You activate the candle by lighting it, which enables creatures within 10 feet of the candle to ignore the cold while within range. Creatures in the area gain cold resistance 10. In addition, a creature taking [persistent cold damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) that is in or enters the area can immediately attempt a DC 15 flat check to end the persistent damage. A given creature can gain this flat check only once from a single _thawing candle_. Once lit, the candle burns for 10 minutes. If extinguished, it can't be relit.

May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate **Source** [Pathfinder #192: Worst of All Possible Worlds](/Sources.aspx?ID=203) pg. 71 **Usage** carried --- _The Avalanche_ represents unmitigated disasters, destruction that overruns all in its path. As long as _The Avalanche_ is invested, you gain a +1 item bonus to damage rolls with Strikes that inflict bludgeoning damage. This increases to a +2 item bonus if you're at least 14th level, and a +3 item bonus if you're at least 18th level. **Activate** envision, Interact; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You wave the card in the air and hurl staggering volumes of ice, snow, and rocks out into the world. This magical avalanche buries your foes. Choose up to 4 creatures within 60 feet, each of whom must attempt a Reflex save against your class DC. Regardless of their saving throw, the creature's space becomes [greater difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=453) from the mounds of ice, snow, and rubble. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes 5d8 bludgeoning damage and is [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) into an adjacent space of its choice.
**Failure** The creature takes 10d8 bludgeoning damage, is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31), and is [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=33).
**Critical Failure** The creature takes 20d8 bludgeoning damage, is knocked prone, and is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24).

---

_The Bear_ represents brute force applied to solve unusual problems. As long as you have _The Bear_ invested, you can use [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks to [Tumble Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=29) or [Squeeze](/Actions.aspx?ID=31).

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per minute;  **Requirements** Your last action was a successful melee Strike; **Effect** You attempt to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=35), [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38), or [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40) the creature you hit with the successful Strike, even if you have no hand free. You gain a +2 status bonus to your check. If you Grapple using a weapon, you can Strike with the weapon only if it has the [grapple](/Traits.aspx?ID=184) trait and you Strike the [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20) target, or if you cease Grabbing with the weapon. After the effect of the initial Grapple ends, you can't keep a target grabbed with a weapon that lacks the grapple trait. The status bonus increases to +3 if you're at least 17th level.

_The Betrayal_ represents selfishness and envy, twisting outcomes toward unfavorable or even devastating results. You gain a +2 item bonus on [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks made to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) or [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=48). This increases to a +3 bonus if you are at least 17th level.

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate</spoilers>

<trait label="Harrow Court" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=496" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** carried

</row>

<row gap="medium">

---

_The Carnival_ represents false dreams. When you have _The Carnival_ invested, your flat check DCs to obtain reliable information from [divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47) effects (such as [_augury_](/Spells.aspx?ID=15) or [_read fate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=445), or the activation of this card) are reduced by 2 (but not to less than 2). Casting a divination effect with a flat check, whether or not the flat check succeeds, gives a series of subtly different visions that don't confuse the meaning but make you [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) for 1 round. If you're at least 17th level, the flat check is instead reduced by 3.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision ([divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47), [prediction](/Traits.aspx?ID=132)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You peer into the future and witness yourself walking through a colorful but vaguely sinister carnival, meeting a variety of strange people. One of these people looks more genuine than the others and resembles someone you're likely to meet for the first time in the next 24 hours (if anyone). This resemblance might be metaphorical, such a clown signifying someone who is silly or a stilt-walker representing someone who is tall. You also get a sense for whether this person can be trusted, should be distrusted, or neither, based on how they're most likely to interact with you and your allies. The GM decides who this new person might be, then rolls a secret DC 6 flat check. On a failure, the result is always “neither,” making it hard to determine whether a “neither” result is accurate.

</column>

_The Courtesan_ represents political intrigue and social niceties. As long as _The Courtesan_ is invested, you gain a +2 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50). This increases to a +3 item bonus if you are at least 17th level.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You pass the card over your face and become exactly who you need to be; you cast [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=159). The level of the spell is one-half your level, rounded down (minimum 6th level). You can change your appearance again at any time during the duration by using a three-action activity, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait. While under these effects, your [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) are one degree of success greater when you use them against a creature that is a lower level than yourself.

As long as it is invested, _The Cyclone_ bolsters you with helpful winds that grant you a +2 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks made to [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=33), [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=36), [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=37), and [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=41). This increases to a +3 item bonus if you are at least 17th level.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You cast [_whirlwind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1033). You do not treat the squares in the _whirlwind_ as difficult terrain, but all other creatures do. The level of the spell is one-half your level, rounded down (minimum 8th level), and the save DC is your class DC.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 25"
    pfs=""
>
[The Deck of Destiny](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2531)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Stolen Fate</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #192: Worst of All Possible Worlds](/Sources.aspx?ID=203) pg. 71

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Composed of 54 cards that are powerful in their own right, the _Deck of Destiny_ epitomizes the powers of the harrow and divination. The deck only has its full suite of abilities while complete. Completing the deck requires all 54 cards to be placed together and shuffled into their complete state over the span of 1 minute; the cards merely being in proximity of each other is not enough to complete the deck. Once complete, the deck can be invested normally.

 While the complete deck is on your person or in hand and invested, you gain a natural insight into events to be. Any [divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47) effects you create become heightened to 10th level for the purpose of determining their counteract level. Additionally, divination effects you create gain a +4 item bonus to their DC and to spell attack rolls. The deck also helps you maintain control of your own fate, granting you immunity to fortune and misfortune effects, though you can be affected by such effects if you wish.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> envision (daily preparations);     **Effect** When you perform your daily preparations, you can share the _Deck of Destiny_ with your companions, allowing them to invest a hand of up to 5 cards each as if they carried the cards. When one of your companions activates one of their invested cards, an illusory image of the card appears in their hand, but the card's effects are otherwise unaltered. This lasts until the next time you perform your daily preparations.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> envision;   **Trigger** A creature you can see within 60 feet is about to attempt a check;  **Effect** You quickly draw a card to alter the triggering creature's fate. Choose either weal or woe. With weal (a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76) effect), the triggering creature rolls twice and takes the better result on their check. With woe (a [misfortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=110) effect), the triggering creature is forced to roll twice and take the worse result. If the card you drew is related to the check, such as drawing a card from the suit of shields for a Fortitude saving throw or a card from the suit of crowns for a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) check, the creature is affected further. When choosing weal, the creature gains a +4 circumstance bonus to the triggering check. When faced with woe, the triggering creature takes a –4 circumstance penalty to the triggering check. Regardless of whether they faced weal or woe, the triggering creature becomes temporarily immune to this ability for 24 hours.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> envision, Interact;     **Effect** You call upon the deck in an attempt to put an end to a creature's life by visiting upon them a particularly grisly fate. Choose a creature within 60 feet. The deck casts [_phantasmal killer_](/Spells.aspx?ID=219) (DC 50, heightened to 10th level) on that creature. This effect doesn't have the [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=92), or [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) traits, as it actually alters reality to rewrite a creature's doom. Regardless of the results, the creature becomes temporarily immune to this effect for 1 week.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 1 hour (envision, Interact);  **Frequency** once per year;   **Effect** You attempt to undo a creature's untimely death and return them to life. The deck performs a 10th-level [resurrect](/Rituals.aspx?ID=20) ritual. This ritual doesn't have any cost and doesn't require any secondary casters. Instead, you are the primary caster and must attempt a DC 50 [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) check to complete the ritual as you perform a harrowing, perform that same harrowing in reverse in an attempt to pull back the threads of fate, and perform one final harrowing to “rewrite” the target's destiny.

**Destruction** The _Deck of Destiny_ is inherently connected to the fate of Golarion. If the deck is used in a harrow reading to determine the destiny of the entire planet, or if the planet itself is destroyed or removed from this reality, the cards crumble to dust after the harrowing is complete or the planet is gone.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

_The Demon's Lantern_ represents trickery and feats of legerdemain. As long as you have _The Demon's Lantern_ invested, you gain a +2 item bonus to checks made to [Conceal an Object](/Actions.aspx?ID=61), [Palm an Object](/Actions.aspx?ID=67), or [Steal](/Actions.aspx?ID=68). This increases to a +3 item bonus if you are at least 17th level.

If your saving throw is higher than the attack roll for the triggering attack, it misses. If the attack misses, the attacker is [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) until the end of your next turn.
