>
[Thrower's Bandolier](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2313)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 146

**Price** 60 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This bandolier is covered in straps and pouches capable of holding up to 2 Bulk of one-handed [thrown](/Traits.aspx?ID=195) weapons. A _thrower's bandolier_ has a [_+1 weapon potency_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=281) rune etched into it, and it can be etched with runes as though it were a one-handed thrown weapon. When you invest the _thrower's bandolier_, you can attune it to all the weapons sheathed in it (this ends any previous attunements made with the bandolier). Whenever you draw a weapon from the bandolier, the bandolier's runes are replicated onto that weapon. Any runes already on the weapon are suppressed, and any runes previously replicated to a different weapon in this way are removed, returning it to normal.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))    **Effect** All weapons attuned to the bandolier, not including any weapons you're currently wielding, return to the bandolier.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Throwing Shield](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1561)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Adjustment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=380" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Knights of Lastwall](/Sources.aspx?ID=123) pg. 87

**Price** 5 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** applied to a buckler or shield

</row>

**Access** Knights of Lastwall have access to this item.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These special straps and weightings fit over a shield or buckler, but not a tower shield. They are designed to let you doff and throw the shield in one swift movement. You can quickly remove the shield by spending a free action as part of the Strike to throw the shield. When thrown in this way, the shield is a martial thrown weapon that deals 1d6 bludgeoning damage and has the [thrown 20 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=195) trait. A shield with the throwing shield attachment can't have any attached weapons, such as [shield spikes](/Weapons.aspx?ID=42) or a [shield boss](/Weapons.aspx?ID=41), and the adjustments to make it more aerodynamic make it slightly less sturdy, reducing its Hardness by 1.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

This small box contains a clockwork mechanism that rhythmically thumps the ground, allowing creatures with [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=40) to detect it at up to double their usual range.     right="Item 5"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Thunder Helm](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1593)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Outlaws of Alkenstar</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #179: Cradle of Quartz](/Sources.aspx?ID=122) pg. 78

**Price** 160 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn headwear

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The creator of the original _thunder helm_ tried and failed time and again to craft a reliable, helmet-mounted firearm that enabled hands-free gunplay, but even after resorting to magical enhancements, they were never quite able to realize their vision. The allure of the _thunder helm_ continues to compel certain mindsets in the Mana Wastes, and these items continue to be crafted to this day.

 A _thunder helm_ appears as a cylindrical iron helmet adorned with a crown-like display of gun barrels extending out in all directions. A slit in the front allows for limited visibility, while sound is muffled by the inner lining. As long as a creature wears a _thunder helm_, it takes a –1 circumstance penalty to [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16) and [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163) Perception checks but also gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against auditory and visual effects.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The helm's gun barrels swivel and aim randomly, then conjure enough gunpowder and bullets to fire in all directions around you. Every creature within a 20-foot emanation takes 4d6 piercing damage (DC 19 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). When determining a creature's resistance or immunity to this damage, use the weaker of the target's resistance or immunity to piercing or bludgeoning.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

This _[+2 greater resilient ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2804) [greater electricity-resistant ](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2788) [chain mail](/Armor.aspx?ID=46)_ is adorned with two golden thunderbolts, one along each forearm. Even on a seemingly cloudless day, you can raise your arms to the heavens and draw down a bolt of lightning upon yourself, empowering your armor and blasting your enemies.

**Activate—Call Down Lightning** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You conjure a bolt of electricity down onto yourself, dealing 6d6 electricity damage to all creatures in a 10-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387). Additionally, for the next minute, whenever a creature touches you or hits you with a melee unarmed attack or a non-reach melee weapon attack, it takes 1d8 electricity damage.

**Usage** worn shoes

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Unassuming in appearance, these slippers indicate their nature only with a signature strip of yellow stitching. You gain a +2 item bonus to [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) checks.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You move like the wind, with precision and speed. You Stride up to 60 feet; this movement doesn't trigger reactions. When you stop, if you've moved at least 30 feet from where you started, you release a thunderous 5-foot emanation that deals 2d6 bludgeoning damage and 2d6 sonic damage with a DC 25 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save. A creature that critically fails its save is also knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 5"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Thundercrasher](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1894)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 39

**Price** 155 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Blunderbuss](/Weapons.aspx?ID=196)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

While looking straight down the barrel of this _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [blunderbuss](/Weapons.aspx?ID=196)_, the spark gun's magical core is visible amid several reflectors. All damage dealt by a _thundercrasher_ is sonic damage. On a critical hit, the target must succeed at a Fortitude save against your class DC or be [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8) for 1 minute.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You overload the _thundercrasher_ to emit chaotic sonic frequencies that soften earth and stone. When you next fire the _thundercrasher_ it also partially liquefies any natural earth or stone surfaces within range of its [scatter](/Traits.aspx?ID=413) trait, making the area difficult terrain.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 11"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Thundering Fury Dadao](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3166)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Sonic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=697" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #199: To Bloom Below the Web](/Sources.aspx?ID=225) pg. 75

**Price** 2,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Greatsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=24)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This massive, curved blade roars when it crashes down on opponents, seemingly intent on subduing them with sheer force. It's said materials for the first thundering fury dadaos came from the hide of Yorak, the Horned Thunder, a legendary kaiju that roams the Shanguang desert. The lack of embellishments on this _+2 striking [thundering](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2850) [greatsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=379)_ belies a weapon of deadly efficacy. 

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You infuse the _thundering fury dadao_ with the speed of lightning and the force of thunder. The weapon gains the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=526) and [forceful](/Traits.aspx?ID=611) traits for one round. You can [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) this activation for up to 1 minute.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Tidal Crossbow](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3211)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Water" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=732" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 103

**Price** 2,800 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Crossbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=425)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The beak and talons of a tidehawk form the triggering mechanism of this [+2](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2830) [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [crossbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=425). Its grip is constantly damp, though this doesn’t affect your ability to keep ahold of the weapon. When used in aquatic combat, a _tidal crossbow_ doesn’t have its range increments halved. A _tidal crossbow_ deals 1d4 additional bludgeoning damage on a successful Strike. On a critical hit, the bow’s additional damage is instead 1d4 bludgeoning splash damage, and the target must succeed at a DC 31 Reflex save or be pushed back 5 feet. The bow critical specialization effect applies to creatures with the water trait even if it wouldn’t normally.

**Activate—Typhoon Swell** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645), [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=732)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The tidal crossbow produces a torrent of water in a 30-foot [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388), dealing 8d6 bludgeoning damage (DC 30 basic Fortitude save). Creatures that fail the save are also knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88).

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include the beak, talons, and several watery feathers of a [tidehawk](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1337).

</column>

>
[Tidal Fishhook](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1485)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
<trait label="Water" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=165" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Monsters of Myth](/Sources.aspx?ID=107) pg. 107

**Price** 1,700 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Combat Grapnel](/Weapons.aspx?ID=139)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This _+2 [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [returning](/Equipment.aspx?ID=301) [combat grapnel](/Weapons.aspx?ID=139)_ takes the form of a fishhook made of scavenged bones and stone with a cord of braided water. Attacks with a _tidal fishhook_ don't take any of the normal penalties for fighting underwater. A [broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=2) (but not destroyed) tidal fishhook can be fully repaired by submerging it in an ocean for 1 minute.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact ([teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=156), [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** A _tidal fishhook_ can travel between bodies of water to strike distant foes. You throw the fishhook into a 5-foot square that's fully covered with water, and it emerges to Strike or [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=35) a target from another such square within 60 feet; the squares can be part of the same body of water or different ones. The distance between the bodies of water doesn't count toward the fishhook's range increment. If you successfully Grapple the target as part of this Strike, you can pull yourself along the fishhook's line, teleporting to the secondary body of water.

Rippling water motifs decorate this simple suit of _+1 [resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=279) [full plate](/Armor.aspx?ID=13)_. The plate has been altered for underwater use, so it's check penalty doesn't apply to Acrobatics or Athletics checks in water or similar liquids. While wearing the armor, you gain a +2 item bonus to Athletics checks to [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=39), and you can breathe underwater. 

**Activate—Ride the Waves** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** The ripples on the armor begin to undulate, matching the movement of any nearby water. The armor casts [_water walk_](/Spells.aspx?ID=371) on you. 

**Activate—Submerge** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104), [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127))
 **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You merge with the water for 10 minutes. While merged, you can't move, you can see through the water if it's clear enough, and you can hear what's going on outside of the water. Water typically can't take damage, but if the water you're merged in is subject to electricity damage or an ability or effect that destroys or dries water, you're expelled from the water and take 10d6 damage. [_Control water_](/Spells.aspx?ID=51) expels you without dealing damage.

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 166

**Price** 1,400 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1

**Base Weapon** [Dueling Pistol](/Weapons.aspx?ID=201)

---

This +2 _[striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [fearsome](/Equipment.aspx?ID=731) [dueling pistol](/Weapons.aspx?ID=201)_ is made from fine tigerwood, with the head of a tiger as the muzzle. Beneath the tiger head is a claw shaped [bayonet](/Weapons.aspx?ID=186). One of a set of four guns crafted as a gift to a Zenj family for delivery of rare healing and disease-abating herbs during an outbreak of a deadly disease in the Grand Duchy of Alkenstar, these firearms are now passed down to those who have done brave acts in service to the Zenj people. The flintlock sparks thrown by this weapon take the shape of pouncing tigers and the firearm's report sounds like a tiger's growl. Clever wielders use the firearm's report to panic their prey into mistakes and then pounce for the kill.

 This firearm's bullets deal slashing damage instead of piercing and add an additional 1d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) on a critical hit. This persistent bleed damage causes tiger-claw-shaped wounds to appear on the target.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You capitalize on the fears your firearm engenders, terrifying your foes. Make a ranged Strike with this firearm against a target. If you successfully deal damage to your target, the target is also affected by a 4th-level [_phantasmal killer_](/Spells.aspx?ID=219) with a spell DC of 28. While _phantasmal killer_ typically takes the shape of the target's worst fear, this effect always appears to the target in the form of a majestic and ferocious tiger.

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 261 **Price** 600 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L **Activate**([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) --- This purple potion has a bitter taste and seems to blur with motion. When you drink a time shield potion, you are frozen in time for 2d4 rounds. You can't act or be targeted, you become immune to all effects, and you vanish from your space; as far as the universe is concerned, you simply don't exist as long as the potion lasts. The durations of any effects targeting you when you drink the potion are suspended until it wears off.
Once the potion's duration expires, you return to the normal flow of time and your former space; if that space is now occupied, you get shunted to the nearest unoccupied space. Effects with durations immediately resume affecting you, elapsing as though no time has passed. If you are within the area of an effect created while you were outside of time, you immediately take those effects upon returning. The GM might determine that other changes that occurred while you were outside of time (such as the ground beneath you crumbling) also affect you upon your return.

The durations of any effects targeting you when you drink the potion are suspended until it wears off. May contain spoilers from Revenge of the Runelords **Source** [Pathfinder #221: Into the Apocalypse Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=371) pg. 77 **Price** 68,000 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 **Base Weapon** [Bastard Sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=370) --- _Timeflaying blades_ are forged around shards of collapsed paradoxes. Their existence is largely an enigma. In the furthest corners of esoteric scholarship, they're mentioned in passing or simply alluded to without ever being named outright. They're associated with Stethelos, the legendary city said to lie at the heart of the Dimension of Time, though it's unclear if they were made there, were discovered there, or are bound to return there at the end of time itself. A _timeflaying blade_ is a _+3 greater striking greater [corrosive](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2834) [keen](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2843) [quickstrike](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2844) [orichalcum](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2919) [bastard sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=370)_. Acid damage caused by a timeflaying blade appears not to be caused by liquid, but by the act of material simply eroding away into dust as if thousands of years passed in an instant (this doesn't impact a creature or object's acid immunity, resistance, or weakness, though). **Activate—Flay Time** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), incapacitation, [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per minute; **Effect** Spend 1 Mythic Point. You swing the _timeflaying blade_ through the air as if slicing something while you attempt to sever a creature within 120 feet from time itself. The creature must attempt a DC 43 Will save. **Critical Success** The creature is [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 for 1 round.
**Success** The creature is hurled 1d4 rounds into the future. They disappear in a flash of white light, only to reappear in the same space on their initiative after the duration. If that space is occupied, the creature is shunted harmlessly aside to the closest unoccupied space.
**Failure** As success, but the creature is hurled forward in time 1d4 minutes.
**Critical Failure** As success, but the creature is hurled into an entirely alternate timeline. At your discretion, the creature's gear is left behind in your timeline. Whether or not the creature will ever return to your timeline depends on the GM's whim, but at the very least, it should never return within the span of a year's passing.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 296

**Price** 14 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

You sprinkle these salts onto a single object up to 10 cubic feet in volume and no more than 40 Bulk to preserve it for 1 week. The object doesn't decay, and effects that require the object to be fresh don't count the time passing during this duration as having elapsed. When sprinkled on a corpse, this extends the period in which a creature can be revived by magic as well as the wait time required before a corpse can be targeted again with talking corpse. The salts prevent ordinary pests from consuming the target (such as maggots for a corpse or moths for a piece of clothing). Any creature can use an Interact action to disperse the salts from an unattended object and end this effect.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 89

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All Pathfinder Society agents have access to all uncommon clockwork items and gadgets from Chapters 1 and 2 of this book_

<row gap="medium">

</row>

**Access** Characters from Absalom, New Thassilon, Alkenstar, Dongun Hold, or especially technological regions of Arcadia like the Deadshot Lands have access to uncommon clockwork items from the first two chapters of this book.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Clockwork timepieces come in a variety of sizes and aesthetic styles, but they're all designed to display the accurate time of day down to the second.

 Clockwork timepieces have a 24-hour activation cycle, after which they must wound in a process that takes 1 minute to complete.

</column>

</traits>

Desktop clocks have been designed to be small enough to only take up a quarter of a typical writing desk's surface area, but they're still too bulky and heavy to be lugged around casually.

These towering, ten-foot-tall clocks have been painstakingly handcrafted by skilled artisans and feature loud chimes that can be heard hourly throughout a manor. Owners of grand clocks usually tend to display them prominently in a study, lounge area, or foyer.

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 191 **Price** 24,000 gp **Usage** worn gloves **Bulk** L --- These bronze gauntlets each have a small red gem embedded in the wrist. You gain a +3 item bonus to [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks and a +1 circumstance bonus to Athletics checks to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=35). If you successfully Grapple an enemy that's at least one size category larger than you, the gauntlets dig into it, dealing bludgeoning damage equal to your Strength modifier, plus an additional 2d6 on a critical success. When you invest the gloves, you either increase your Strength score by 2 or increase it to 18, whichever would give you a higher score. **Activate** Interact ([sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147)) **Frequency** once per day; **Requirements** You have two hands free; **Effect** You clap the gauntlets together with a thunderous crack that deals 6d10 sonic damage in a 30-foot emanation. Each creature in the area must attempt a DC 35 Fortitude save. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes half damage.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage and is [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8) for 1 round.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage, is deafened for 1 minute, and is [stunned 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 155, [Pathfinder #169: Kindled Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=94) pg. 75

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn mask

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Colorful, beaded _tlil masks_ are commonly found on the distant continent of Arcadia, but trade between the two regions means that they can also be found in the Mwangi Expanse as curiosities. These masks usually bear floral patterns and attune your senses to plants of all varieties.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Your vision up to 60 feet sees through small amounts of living plant matter as though it were transparent. While this effect is active, creatures can't be [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) from you due to living plants, such as small trees, vines, and grass. This vision also prevents them from [Hiding](/Actions.aspx?ID=62) or [Sneaking](/Actions.aspx?ID=63) past you using only living plants for concealment or cover. Other than the inability to use the cover to Hide or Sneak, this ability doesn't prevent plants from providing [cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=459) to creatures or blocking line of effect. It also doesn't allow you to see through dead plant matter, such as the wooden walls of a building, or thick plant matter, such as the walls of a dungeon built entirely inside an enormous living tree. The effect lasts for 1 minute.

Toad tears can be mixed with any other foodstuff or drink, but the poison can also be ingested as is. The process of refining giant toad poison lessens its deadly qualities, and as a result, toad tears are rarely directly fatal. ---

The primary ingredient of this chalky, plain-tasting blue gruel is the memory-altering cytillesh fungus so prized by [deros](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=388). [Hryngars](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=432) favor toiler's gruel as a primary source of food for their captives, for those who ingest it are robbed of their memories and grow more compliant. Toiler's gruel resets its maximum duration if ingested by a creature already under its effects. Subsequent exposure makes the memory loss of stage 3 cumulative. 

**Saving Throw** DC 19 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 3 days; **Stage 1** [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 (10 minutes); **Stage 2** stupefied 1, and memories of the previous hour are forever eliminated from the victim's consciousness (1 hour); **Stage 3** stupefied 1, and the mold dulls memories of the previous day, forcing the victim to make a DC 19 Will save to recall all but the most simple and routine events during that period (1 day)

This charm is usually worn around the neck or hanging from a belt. It consists of a three-part hourglass with individual glass bulbs filled with sea salts, charcoal ash, and minute slivers of silver. <title
    level="1"
    right="Item 10"
    pfs=""
>
[Tome of Dripping Shadows](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2680)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Sky King's Tomb</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Grimoire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=387" />
<trait label="Illusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=92" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Shadow" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=143" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #195: Heavy is the Crown](/Sources.aspx?ID=210) pg. 81

**Price** 1,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This book constantly drips evanescent tendrils of shadow that seethe and writhe. The tendrils have a will of their own, retreating from light sources and curling toward darkness. While you hold the tome, you gain [darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=415); if you already have darkvision, you gain [greater darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12) instead.

 Preparing spells from this tome strengthens your shadow magic and gives you a greater understanding of shadow spells you add to this tome. Any [shadow](/Traits.aspx?ID=143) spells you prepare from this tome that are at least 2 levels lower than the highest-level spell you can cast are treated as 1 level higher for the purposes of [counteracting](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) them. When you add a shadow spell to this tome, you can prepare heightened versions of that spell up to the highest level of that spell that you are able to cast.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> envision;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** A target of a shadow spell you prepared from the grimoire critically fails a saving throw against the spell;  **Effect** You recall a fragment of the shadow magic that suffuses your target and wrap it around yourself like a caul. The triggering creature's saving throw result is a failure, not a critical failure. For the next minute, you become [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) to all creatures and you are [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) from the triggering creature, regardless of what precise sense it has. If you use a [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=300) against the triggering creature, you become only concealed to it (rather than hidden) at the end of the hostile action.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Tome of Scintillating Sleet](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2184)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Cold" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=27" />
<trait label="Grimoire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=387" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 113

**Price** 430 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The first 12 pages of this tome tell the same story in two languages: 6 pages in [Skald](/Languages.aspx?ID=42) and 6 pages in the ancient [Jotun](/Languages.aspx?ID=8) dialect used by saumen kar, a species of ice-dwelling [humanoids](/Traits.aspx?ID=91). The story is a tale of a saumen kar stricken with snow blindness after spending too long under the sun building snow giants.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** If your next action is to cast a [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555) spell that deals damage, all creatures damaged by the spell are also [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) for 3 rounds by light refracting and reflecting within and around the spell's chilling effects. If an affected creature critically failed its save against the required spell, or if you critically succeeded on your spell attack roll against the creature, it's instead [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) for 1 round and then dazzled for 3 rounds.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Toolkit of Bronze Whispers](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2402)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="No Alignment" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Intelligent" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=280" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 197

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Perception** +12; [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411) vision 30 feet, [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412) hearing 30 feet

**Communication** [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=37) ([Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) and two other common languages)

**Skills** [Clockwork Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) +15, [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) +13, [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) +11

**Int** +4, **Wis** +3, **Cha** +0

**Will** +12 

</column>

---        

Sacred to the faith of [Brigh](/Deities.aspx?ID=33), a _toolkit of bronze whispers_ has been used with such devotion it has developed a consciousness and personality that can be a blessing to a partnered crafter. A _toolkit of bronze whispers_ functions as a set of [sterling artisan's tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3). Such toolkits focus on new creations and enthusiastically suggest crafting techniques to wielders. A _toolkit of bronze whispers_ knows common item formulas of its level or lower and any other formulas the GM chooses. It can teach these formulas. You must still spend the time to copy a formula before you can use it.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 6+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Tooth and Claw Tattoo](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2219)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Tattoo" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=262" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 122

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** tattooed on the body

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This tattoo resembles an animal's fangs, claws, or similar natural weapons, letting you wield such weapons and turn into the same beast. When you receive the tattoo, choose the animal from among the following: ape, bear, bull, canine, cat, deer, frog, shark, or snake. You can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) skill with animals of that kind. This tattoo is usually located on the body part or parts it's meant to transform—on the back of the hands for claws, around the mouth for jaws, on the forehead for horns, and so on.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [morph](/Traits.aspx?ID=657))    **Effect** You gain an [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack matching the tattoo for 1 minute. It has the same damage as your best unarmed attack and has the same traits. Its damage type is bludgeoning for a fist or frog's jaws; piercing for an antler, fangs, horns, or most jaws; or slashing for claws.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=670))    **Effect** The tattoo casts 3rd-rank [_animal form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1440) to transform you into the animal that matches your tattoo.

</column>

fields.text: Item 6+ Tooth and Claw Tattoo Invested Magical Tattoo Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 122 Usage tattooed on the body This tattoo resembles an animal's fangs, claws, or similar natural weapons, letting you wield such weapons and turn into the same beast. When you receive the tattoo, choose the animal from among the following: ape, bear, bull, canine, cat, deer, frog, shark, or snake. You can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the Diplomacy skill with animals of that kind. This tattoo is usually located on the body part or parts it's meant to transform—on the back of the hands for claws, around the mouth for jaws, on the forehead for horns, and so on. Activate Single Action (concentrate, morph) Effect You gain an unarmed attack matching the tattoo for 1 minute. It has the same damage as your best unarmed attack and has the same traits. Its damage type is bludgeoning for a fist or frog's jaws; piercing for an antler, fangs, horns, or most jaws; or slashing for claws. Activate Two Actions (concentrate, polymorph) Effect The tattoo casts 3rd-rank animal form to transform you into the animal that matches your tattoo. Item 6 Tooth and Claw Tattoo Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 122 Price 250 gp Item 8 Tooth and Claw Tattoo (Greater) Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 122 Price 500 gp The tattoo casts 4th-rank animal form instead of 3rd. Item 10 Tooth and Claw Tattoo (Major) Source Treasure Vault (Remastered) pg. 122 Price 1,000 gp The tattoo casts 5th-rank animal form instead of 3rd.

>
[Tooth and Claw Tattoo](/Equipment.aspx?ID=4753)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Tattoo" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=262" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 122

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** tattooed on the body

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This tattoo resembles an animal’s fangs, claws, or similar natural weapons, letting you wield such weapons and turn into the same beast. When you receive the tattoo, choose the animal from among the following: ape, bear, bull, canine, cat, deer, frog, shark, or snake. You can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) skill with animals of that kind. This tattoo is usually located on the body part or parts it’s meant to transform—on the back of the hands for claws, around the mouth for jaws, on the forehead for horns, and so on..

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command ([morph](/Traits.aspx?ID=657))    **Effect** You gain an unarmed attack matching the tattoo for 1 minute. It has the same damage as your best unarmed attack and has the same traits. Its damage type is bludgeoning for a fist or frog’s jaws; piercing for an antler, fangs, horns, or most jaws; or slashing for claws..

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, envision ([polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=670))    **Effect** The tattoo casts 3rd-level [_animal form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1440) to transform you into the animal that matches your tattoo.

Originally used in dental procedures, toothwort numbs the gums by deadening nerves. When the oils are extracted and distilled, toothwort has a secondary reputation among alchemists for enhancing the duration of poisons. When adding toothwort extract to an [alchemical poison](/Equipment.aspx?Category=6&Subcategory=9), you can extend the maximum duration of the poison by 1 round.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Oil" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=121" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 176

**Price** 70 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This slimy gel wriggles to the touch, as if covered by a multitude of imperceptible cilia. If applied to a creature or object no larger than 7 feet in any dimension, the protoplasm shifts it into an [ooze](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=79)-like state for 1 minute, allowing the subject to squash and stretch harmlessly. In this state, a creature that attempts a check to [Squeeze](/Actions.aspx?ID=31) uses the outcome one degree of success better than it rolls and can move its full Speed while Squeezing, and an object can fit through a space 2 feet across. One vial can cover a creature or object of up to Large size, but as each vial is made from a specific ooze, multiple vials can't be combined together to cover a larger object, as the two gels simply negate each other.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

This portable silver anvil has a narrow hoop on one end, through which a long, sturdy chain has been strung. _[Torag's](/Deities.aspx?ID=18) Silver Anvil_ can be wielded as a _+3 [holy](/Equipment.aspx?ID=299) [greater flaming](/Equipment.aspx?ID=295) [greater striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=379) [meteor hammer](/Weapons.aspx?ID=97)_. Outside of combat, the anvil can be used with a hammer as an incredibly effective portable forge, heating up the metal to be forged without a furnace and granting a +3 item bonus to [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) checks involving metalworking. When you use the anvil to successfully [Repair](/Actions.aspx?ID=42) a metal item, the item recovers an additional 10 Hit Points (or an additional 20 on a critical success).

fields.text: Item 18 Torag's Silver Anvil Uncommon Divine Magical Transmutation Source Gods & Magic pg. 123 Price 24,000 gp Usage held in 2 hands Bulk 2 Base Weapon Meteor Hammer Access follower of Torag This portable silver anvil has a narrow hoop on one end, through which a long, sturdy chain has been strung. Torag's Silver Anvil can be wielded as a +3 holy greater flaming greater striking silver meteor hammer . Outside of combat, the anvil can be used with a hammer as an incredibly effective portable forge, heating up the metal to be forged without a furnace and granting a +3 item bonus to Crafting checks involving metalworking. When you use the anvil to successfully Repair a metal item, the item recovers an additional 10 Hit Points (or an additional 20 on a critical success).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 18"
    pfs=""
>
[Tornado Trompo](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1741)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Air" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=5" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Celebrating Hispanic Heritage Month](/Sources.aspx?ID=149)

**Price** 19,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Various runes are carved along the entirety of this wooden top. Spinning the top requires wrapping a thick string around its base and pulling the string in a vigorous motion. Wrapping a string and pulling the string each require an Interact action. The top's magic is connected to the power of the wind, which becomes evident when placed on a surface as it hovers in place.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;    **Requirements** A string is wrapped around the top and you have a hand free; **Effect** You lightly pull on the string and catch the top in your free hand. It spins in place, hovering over your open palm, sharing its power over the winds with you. You gain the effects of [fly](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=136) as long as you keep the top in your hand. You can Release the top at any time to end the effect.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;  **Requirements** A string is wrapped around the top; **Effect** You call upon the top's power and give the string a powerful pull. The top travels across the ground in a 120-foot line. As it does, it unleashes a powerful vortex of winds, becoming a tornado temporarily. This tornado has the effects of [_whirlwind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1033) except that it's not limited by being used outside or in a cramped space and can't be sustained. Creatures in the tornado's path must attempt a DC 38 Reflex save to determine the effects of the tornado. The tornado ends after traveling its full distance, causing any creatures that rose in the air due to a failed save to begin falling immediately.

**Failure** The target falls [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31).
**Critical Failure** The target falls prone and is forced into one of the other squares soaked by the snare.

    level="1"

>
[Toshigami Blossom](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2403)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="No Alignment" url="/Rules.aspx?ID=95" />
<trait label="Intelligent" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=280" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 197

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

<column gap="tiny">

**Perception** +30; [precise](/Rules.aspx?ID=411) vision ([darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=415)) 30 feet, [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412) hearing 30 feet

**Communication** [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=37) ([Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=1) and two other common languages; [_speak with plants_](/Spells.aspx?ID=294))

**Skills** [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) +28, [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9) +32, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) +32

**Int** +6, **Wis** +10, **Cha** +5

**Will** +32 

</column>

---        

An encounter with a [toshigami](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1204), the enigmatic [kami](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=243) who protect cherry trees, is rare, though often sought after and treasured by those who achieve such an encounter. Only a handful of mortals can truthfully claim to have seen a toshigami, let alone met one, though many popular fireside tales tell of virtuous souls receiving a toshigami's blessing to fight for a worthy cause. Such stories have a basis in fact; every so often, a toshigami gives a worthy mortal a flower from their ward, time-locked in perfect bloom and granted sapience. Such _toshigami blossoms_ are more sociable than their creators. Like toshigami, a blossom has a strong curiosity about the mortal world. If you wear a _toshigami blossom_, it can intercede for you, helping you make a good impression.

 A _toshigami blossom_ has the following activations.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The blossom casts [_nature’s pathway_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1613) on you to your specifications. If you teleport through only cherry trees, the spell is cast at 6th rank.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** The blossom casts [_soothing blossoms_](/Spells.aspx?ID=999) to your specifications.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** The blossom sends a flurry of cherry blossoms outward in a 20-foot [burst](/Rules.aspx?ID=2385) that lasts 1 round. You and your allies can see through these blossoms. To all other creatures, creatures within the cloud of blossoms become [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62), and creatures outside the cloud become concealed to creatures within it. When you or an ally succeeds with a Strike against a creature in the blossoms, the Strike deals an additional 1d6 [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) damage and an additional 1d6 [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) damage to living creatures, or an additional 1d6 [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509) damage to [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<column gap="tiny">

**Perception** +30; precise vision ([darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59)) 30 feet, [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=2407) hearing 30 feet

**Communication** [telepathy](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=79) ([Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155) and two other common languages; [_speak with plants_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1681))

**Skills** [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) +28, [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42) +32, [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) +32

**Int** +6, **Wis** +10, **Cha** +5

**Will** +32 

</column>

---        

An encounter with a [toshigami](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1204), the enigmatic [kami](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=604) who protect cherry trees, is rare, though often sought after and treasured by those who achieve such an encounter. Only a handful of mortals can truthfully claim to have seen a toshigami, let alone met one, though many popular fireside tales tell of virtuous souls receiving a toshigami’s blessing to fight for a worthy cause. Such stories have a basis in fact; every so often, a toshigami gives a worthy mortal a flower from their ward, time-locked in perfect bloom and granted sapience. Such _toshigami blossoms_ are more sociable than their creators. Like toshigami, a blossom has a strong curiosity about the mortal world. If you wear a _toshigami blossom_, it can intercede for you, helping you make a good impression.

A _toshigami blossom_ has the following activations.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The blossom casts [_tree stride_](/Spells.aspx?ID=343) on you to your specifications. If you target only cherry trees, the spell is cast at 6th level.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> command, envision;  **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** The blossom casts [_soothing blossoms_](/Spells.aspx?ID=999) to your specifications.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;  **Frequency** once per minute;   **Effect** The blossom sends a flurry of cherry blossoms outward in a 20-foot [burst](/Rules.aspx?ID=2385) that lasts 1 round. You and your allies can see through these blossoms. To all other creatures, creatures within the cloud of blossoms become [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62), and creatures outside the cloud become concealed to creatures within it. When you or an ally succeeds with a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) against a creature in the blossoms, the Strike deals an additional 1d6 mental damage and an additional 1d6 negative damage to living creatures, or an additional 1d6 positive damage to [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722).

---

Alchemical reagents add punch to tracker's stew: a rich, fiery mixture of tomatoes, ground nuts, onions, and tubers, often with poultry added. It's usually served with or over rice or noodles. Once you've eaten the stew, it improves your ability to sense and follow tracks for 24 hours or until you make your next daily preparations, whichever comes first. You gain a +1 item bonus to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) checks to [Cover Tracks](/Actions.aspx?ID=65) and [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=66). You can do either while moving at full speed or both while moving at half speed.

Used covertly by assassins and spies, this pair of fulus stick to one another when created but can be easily separated. Affix one fulu to a target before activating its pair. When activated, the unaffixed fulu flutters toward the affixed one at a Speed of 30 feet per round, traveling for up to 1 hour and fluttering more rapidly the closer it comes to its pair. The unaffixed fulu always moves in a straight line toward the affixed fulu; it can’t solve mazes or find its way through winding paths.

</row>

<row gap="medium">

---

Crafters choose tattoos that represent their dedication and skill in their chosen field. Such tattoos might adorn the arm, fingers, or eyes, and they take the form of artistic patterns or depict tools of the trade, such as anvils, paintbrushes, or trowels. You gain a +2 item bonus to [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) checks. Furthermore, when you roll a critical failure on a Crafting check to [Earn Income](/Actions.aspx?ID=23), treat it as a failure instead.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 1 minute ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The tattoo casts [_creation_](/Spells.aspx?ID=54). You choose the item and its appearance, and whether the spell is 4th or 5th rank.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Tattoo" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=262" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 243

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** tattooed on the body

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Many cultures of Golarion have a tattoo that is believed to turn away harm. As such, _warding tattoos_ often resemble whichever dangers are most common to the culture, such as a wild beast in the forests of Kyonin, a whirlpool in the high seas of the Shackles, or the stylized face of a [demon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=387) in the Sarkoris Scar. 

**Activate—Inked Safeguard** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** An enemy, hazard, or the environment makes an attack against your AC, requires you to attempt a saving throw, or causes you to take damage automatically;  **Effect** Until the end of the current turn, against the triggering effect, you gain a +1 status bonus to AC and saving throws and gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) 2 to the triggering damage.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Price** 250 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

You gain resistance 2 to damage from hazardous terrain and environmental hazards at all times, which increases to 5 when the tattoo is activated.

<title

pfs="Standard"

Wave Warding Tattoo
</title>

</traits>

**Price** 220 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

In addition to the normal triggers, you can activate the tattoo when you enter an environment where you can’t breathe. When you activate the tattoo, it casts _air bubble_ on you, in addition to the other effects.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 0"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Traitor's Ring](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1630)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 83

**Price** 1 gp, 5 sp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

**Access** Member of a secret society

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This ring has a thick band supporting a square-cut gem that can be customized to the buyer's preference. The thickness of the band allows it to be taken to any jeweler or blacksmith to be adjusted to different hands or fingers from the original make. There is a tiny clasp at the side of the gem that, when pressed, opens the gem, revealing a small, hinged compartment. This compartment is designed to hold one dose of poison, allowing wearers to slip the contents of the ring into the food or drink of an intended target. The compartment can be closed again by gently pressing the gem back into place. Noticing the compartment requires a DC 15 Perception check for anyone inspecting the ring.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

The compartment can be closed again by gently pressing the gem back into place. Noticing the compartment requires a DC 15 Perception check for anyone inspecting the ring.

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 31

<row gap="medium">
**Ammunition** any

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Two Actions" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_Transposition ammunition_ has a milky-white cast and will sometimes shift position subtly of its own accord. When you activate the ammunition, instead of making your Strike against a foe, you fire _transposition ammunition_ at any unoccupied square you can see within your weapon's first range increment and succeed without making an attack roll. You pull yourself through the [Astral Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=8), teleporting along with any items you are holding into the square where you shot the ammunition. If this would carry along any other creature (even one in an [extradimensional](/Traits.aspx?ID=67) space), the activation fails.

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Traveler's Any-Tool](/Equipment.aspx?ID=268)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 576

**Price** 200 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 2 hands

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Before it’s activated, this item appears to be an ash rod capped with steel on either end.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;     **Effect** You imagine a specific simple tool, and the any-tool transforms into it. (Usually, you can choose from a tool listed in Chapter 6). This transforms the wooden portion into any haft and the metal caps into spades, hammer heads, or the like, allowing for most basic tools but nothing more complex. You can return the item to its rod form with an Interact action.

These cloaks are designed to accommodate long treks through various climates. Traveler's cloaks for hot climates might be bleached white and created from lighter materials, while those intended for cold climates are made of thicker materials and have linings intended to retain heat. While wearing a traveler's cloak for the appropriate type of weather, increase the time it takes to become [fatigued from temperature effects](/Rules.aspx?ID=642) by 2 hours. A traveler's cloak has no effect at extreme or incredible temperatures.

</row>

---

This fulu shows a series of constellations and arrows depicting astronomical movements through the night sky. When you activate a _traveler’s fulu_, the magic infuses your mind with sensations of deja vu, as if you’d been in this region before. Your attempt to [Sense Direction](/Actions.aspx?ID=2406) functions as if you have a compass, and you use the outcome one degree of success better than the result of your [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) check to Sense Direction, or by two degrees of success if you’re a master in Survival.

This more robust assembly is well suited for longer travel and all manner of adventuring. As with the [traveler's chair](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1356), small mechanisms built into the wheels and support struts allow the user to traverse up and down stairs without any additional difficulty (though moving up stairs is still difficult terrain, just like for other adventurers) and move without additional difficulty through ladders, uneven ground, and other common adventuring terrain.

[Tremorsensors](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2168)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Adjustment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=380" />
<trait label="Mechanical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=105" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 109

**Price** 100 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** affixed to armor

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These small, metallic devices resemble squashed spheres. They each contain a tiny gyroscope that's incredibly sensitive to vibrations in the earth. While typically worn on one's footwear, the device can be affixed to any part of your armor.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You stomp a foot, clap your hands, or create some other source of sound, gaining [tremorsense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=40) as an [imprecise sense](/Rules.aspx?ID=412) with a range of 20 feet for the next 10 minutes.

    level="1"
    right="Item 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Triangular Teeth](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2221)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Tattoo" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=262" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 122

**Price** 33 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** tattooed on the body

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Rows of triangles symbolizing shark teeth protect you from danger and enable you to take fierce retaliation against those who try to harm you. Seafarers, especially those on the seas of Minata, wear these tattoos in patterns, with multiple rows of regular triangles. You gain a +1 item bonus to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) checks to navigate bodies of water.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You would be hit by an attack against your AC;  **Effect** You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC against the attack, or a +2 circumstance bonus if the attacker is in water or has the [amphibious](/Traits.aspx?ID=207), [aquatic](/Traits.aspx?ID=168), or [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165) trait. Whether the attack hits or misses, you gain a +2 status bonus to damage with the next Strike you make against the attacker before the end of your next turn.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

Seafarers, especially those on the seas of Minata, wear these tattoos in patterns, with multiple rows of regular triangles. You gain a +1 item bonus to Survival checks to navigate bodies of water. Activate Reaction command; Frequency once per day; Trigger You would be hit by an attack against your AC; Effect You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC against the attack, or a +2 circumstance bonus if the attacker is in water or has the amphibious, aquatic, or water trait. Whether the attack hits or misses, you gain a +2 status bonus to damage with the next Strike you make against the attacker before the end of your next turn.

This item looks like a normal trident carved with Gozren motifs. If thrown without being activated, it wobbles in the air and fails to strike true. **Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 300 **Price** 15 gp --- You set a cunning wire to trip a creature. A Medium or smaller creature that enters this snare's square must attempt a DC 21 Reflex save.
If you want to create a trip snare to trip a larger creature, you must create a group of contiguous snares of a length equal to the edge of that larger creature's space, and the creature must be moving such that it moves into the full set of snares. For example, three trip snares in a 15-foot-line can trip a Huge creature coming down a corridor into the line of snares. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the start of its next turn.
**Failure** The creature falls [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88).
**Critical Failure** The creature falls prone and takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage.

</row>

<row gap="medium">

---

This arrow unspools a line of wire as its flies at its target. The wire animates as it hits a target and attempts to wrap around its legs before vanishing a moment later. If you can apply the bow's [critical specialization effect](/Rules.aspx?ID=235), you can choose to knock the target [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) instead of pinning the target. If you cannot apply the bow's critical specialization effect, you can instead attempt to use the arrow to [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40) with the [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) skill as if the bow had the [trip](/Traits.aspx?ID=196) weapon trait. The arrow's unwieldy nature halves its weapon's range increment.

---

Tripods are designed for use with [kickback](/Traits.aspx?ID=409) weapons, as a way for gunslingers with lower strength to accurately use these more powerful weapons by sacrificing mobility instead. They can be set up and attached to a firearm with a single Interact action using one hand, setting the tripod in your square. If the kickback weapon requires two hands, you can change your grip on the weapon as part of this action. While this sturdy piece of engineering is in use, you don't take the –2 penalty for firing a kickback weapon, even if your Strength isn't high enough to avoid the penalty. However, you must retrieve the tripod with a single Interact action before you can move the firearm to a different position. Normally, when you're [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39), you become observed if you do anything except Hide, [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=63), or Step. However, deploying or retrieving a tripod with an Interact action doesn't automatically make you observed, so long as you don't set up or remove the tripod when it's in a spot where creatures can see the tripod itself.

[Troll Hide](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1986)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=89" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 65

**Price** 6,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Hide Armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=44)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Tissue from a living [forest troll](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3219) has been integrated through this [hide armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=44). This armor has two organic receptacles on its back that can each hold a single [elixir of life](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3308). One elixir takes 3 Interact actions to install. For the armor to function properly, each elixir must be the same level.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))   **Requirements** Two elixirs of life are installed in the armor; **Effect** Regenerating tissue from the armor fills your wounds for 8 rounds. At the start of each of your turns, you regain Hit Points equal to the level of the loaded elixirs. Each time you regain at least 13 Hit Points from the armor, you regrow one damaged or ruined organ. During a round that you regain 9 or more Hit Points from the armor, you can reattach severed body parts by spending an Interact action to hold the body part to the area it was severed from. If you take [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586) or [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) damage, the armor deactivates until the end of your next turn. (Similar armor from other types of trolls might be deactivated by different damage types.) In the event the armor itself is damaged, it will restore its own Hit Points before it resumes healing you. The activation uses up the elixirs, and the armor can’t be activated again until two new ones are installed.

This suit of _[+1](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2804) [hide armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=44)_ is sickly green and covered in thick warts and nodules, fashioned from the hide of a [trollhound](/Monsters.aspx?ID=835) and imbued with some of the beast’s vitality. Wearing this armor gives you a –1 circumstance penalty to all checks made using [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) to interact with [trolls](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=478) and a +1 circumstance bonus to Diplomacy checks used to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) in communities traditionally plagued by troll attacks.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> Interact;   **Trigger** You take damage from a melee attack while you have half or fewer of your normal maximum Hit Points;  **Effect** Your body knits itself back together, healing you for 3d8 Hit Points.

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include the hides of at least two [trollhounds](/Monsters.aspx?ID=835).

---

This jaunty cap can take the form and color of any type of hat you wish upon investing the item, but it always has a peacock feather jutting out from one side. You gain a +2 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) and [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks while wearing the cap. When you invest the cap, you either increase your Charisma modifer by 1 or increase it to +4, whichever would give you a higher value.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You cast [_hypnotize_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1564) (DC 37).

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Picking the feather from your cap, you throw it toward a target, casting [_prismatic spray_](/Spells.aspx?ID=233) (DC 35).

---

When opened, this grimoire has unlimited pages that, oddly, seem almost eager to transcribe spells. Unlike most grimoires, it has no limits to its number of spells. The grimoire’s eagerness to contain your spells grants you a +1 item bonus to checks to [Learn a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2366) if you do so by transcribing the spell into the grimoire. If you use the grimoire during your daily preparations and are capable of preparing spells of the appropriate rank, the grimoire’s nature leaks into your mind, allowing you to prepare an additional 1st-rank spell.

---

This pair of huge wings is crafted from numerous feathers made of a lightweight, golden magical alloy. When activated, the wings emit a melodic sound and a shimmering glow. 

**Activate—Assisted Flight** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** For the next 10 minutes, you can [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298) 20 feet, using the wings to propel yourself. You must land on a space with solid ground. For the duration, you also emit a [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2402) in a 20-foot radius and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2403) for the next 20 feet. You take a –2 item penalty to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) checks to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=2404) and [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=2405).

---

This amulet bears the true name of a single creature with a level no higher than the item's level. These amulets are typically made of gold and engraved, but could be made of anything, including simple clay. The name is clearly visible, though only to you, and only while you have the amulet invested.

If you can read the language in which the name is written, that creature always takes the effects of [_invoke true name_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1065) against your spells (with a spell level equal to half the item's level, rounded up). In addition, when the creature uses any magical effect against you, you can immediately attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) it using [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Domains.aspx?ID=22), [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120), or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) for the counteract check and the _true name amulet's_ level to determine the counteract level. Legendary amulets bearing the true names of creatures of level 21+ may exist.

---

Concentrated wolfsbane and other anti-shapechanger reagents fill trueshape bombs. These bombs grant an item bonus to attack rolls and deal poison damage, [persistent poison damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29), and poison splash damage, according to their type. If the primary target is under the effects of a [morph](/Traits.aspx?ID=113) or [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=127) effect, it must succeed at a Fortitude saving throw at the bomb's listed DC, or else the effects end and the creature returns to its normal form. Targets taking persistent poison damage from this bomb must succeed at another Fortitude saving throw at the same DC to change shape using a morph or polymorph effect. The persistent damage can last up to 1 minute.

---

A trundle wheel is used to measure distance. It is a wheel attached to a handle so that it rolls along the ground. The wheel is often covered with leather or a rough metal to allow better grip on a surface and ensure it maintains traction. It’s of an exact circumference, usually a yard or five feet. Each time it makes a complete rotation it makes an audible click so the user knows they have gone exactly that distance and can count the clicks to determine a longer distance traveled.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 171

**Price** 9 gp

<row gap="medium">
**Ammunition** any

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><row><actions string="Free Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This ammunition was developed in Dongun Hold to minimize casualties to friendly fire, and is always marked by a burnished copper head or tip so it can be easily identified. Before you can fire a _trustworthy round_, you must call out a target. You don't need to specify a name; the target could be “The angry tiger attacking our group on the left.” The round will only hit the specified target and will turn to gossamer dust midair if it misses the intended target or comes into contact with anything else; this also prevents abilities that redirect attacks. The round doesn't have any capabilities beyond your own to determine whether someone is who you think they are, so you can't use it to determine a disguised creature's identity. If you specify a target of “Seltyiel” and shoot someone disguised as Seltyiel who you thought was Seltyiel, the attack will still hit, whereas if you were about to hit a disguised Seltyiel who you didn't recognize to be Seltyiel, the round would dissolve.

</column>

---

This sparkling purple belt was made for the youngest member of a family of jugglers and tumblers who traveled with the Crascondo Company. The thought was this would allow the child to safely participate with their elder siblings and cousins, but the belt found itself being “loaned” more and more often to dare-taking elders in the troupe. The _tumbler’s belt_ grants a +2 item bonus to [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) checks, and whenever you critically succeed at a check to [Tumble Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=2370), you gain a +10-foot item bonus to your [Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2894) until the end of your turn. While wearing the _tumbler’s belt_, you’re not [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) while you [Balance](/Actions.aspx?ID=2369).

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> Land With Grace;  **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You're falling;  **Effect** Treat your fall as if it were 120 feet shorter. Regardless of whether you take damage or not from the fall, you land on your feet.

[Twilight Lantern](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1451)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Strength of Thousands</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Light" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=100" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #172: Secrets of the Temple City](/Sources.aspx?ID=102) pg. 76

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This elegant hooded lantern is made from onyx-black metal. In dim light, flecks of white metal speckled within the lantern's housing resemble stars in a night sky. The lantern uses oil as a standard hooded lantern, except that any light the lantern emits is converted into magical light similar to moonlight. This magical moonlight is always dim light.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> envision;     **Effect** You concentrate on the lantern's light and reduce or increase its radius. The light can have a minimum radius of 5 feet and a maximum radius equal to double the light's standard radius.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision, Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You raise the lantern and unleash a beam of powerful moonlight, targeting a [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=39) effect within 60 feet. The lantern attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the effect with a counteract modifier of +10.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 5"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Twilight Tattoo](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3765)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Tattoo" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=262" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Shining Kingdoms](/Sources.aspx?ID=265) pg. 52

**Price** 125 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

**Access** You’re a member of the Twilight Talons.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This tattoo of a black eagle gripping a sword and arrows in its talons identifies the bearer as a member of the Twilight Talons. Agents typically keep the tattoo hidden unless they need to prove their identity to another member. The bearer gains a +1 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks.

**Activate—Fade** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629))    **Effect** You hide your tattoo from view. The tattoo is [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=83) for 1 day and can’t be detected by effects such as [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1485) and [_read aura_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1646). You can [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) this effect. 

**Activate—Inscribe** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=629), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You lay your hand on a piece of text, and your tattoo makes a perfect copy of it, storing it as a ring of swirling letters surrounding the design. The tattoo can hold text equivalent to two pages of a book, a single [scroll](/Traits.aspx?ID=688), or a similar area of other surfaces, though it doesn’t replicate any magical effect or other special properties of the original words. You can [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) this effect, and when you Dismiss it, the tattoo copies the original text onto a blank writing surface you’re touching.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title

    right="Item 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Twining Chains](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1431)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Adjustment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=380" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 104

**Price** 5 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** applied to armor

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This set of chains is completely covered with spikes and sharp blades. Not balanced for weapon use, twining chains are instead wrapped around a user's body as a deterrent to attackers—and, for some, a fashion statement. While wearing twining chains, you gain the Thorns reaction. In addition to their dangers, twining chains' weight also increases your armor's Bulk by 1, Strength entry value by 2, and check penalty by 2.

 **Thorns** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** You are hit by an [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack; **Effect** You twist to harm your attacker with your chains' spikes and blades. Make an attack roll against the triggering attacker using your unarmed attack modifier. On a hit, the attacking creature takes 1d6 piercing damage. This damage increases to 2d6 damage if the armor has a _[+1 potency_ rune](/Equipment.aspx?ID=278), 3d6 damage if the armor has a _+2 potency_ rune, or 4d6 damage if the armor has a _+3 potency_ rune. However, whether you hit or miss, you take piercing damage equal to the number of d6s of piercing damage you would deal your attacker.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

The body of a fearsome [tyrannosaurus](/Monsters.aspx?ID=123) is shrunken and contained in this bottle, its desiccated form barely constrained within the glass.
